name: Jubilees
sourceNote: Translated from the Ethiopic (Ge‘ez) text of Jubilees, chiefly as edited by August Dillmann, *Das Buch der Jubiläen* (1859), and R. H. Charles, *The Ethiopic Version of the Hebrew Book of Jubilees* (1895), with the surviving Latin fragments (Ceriani, 1861) and the Hebrew fragments from Qumran as reported in the standard editions, and as they were available to the translator through Charles’s critical apparatus; none was checked against the manuscripts. The English is new. R. H. Charles’s English translation (1902; revised 1913), which is in the public domain, was consulted for the readings of the Ethiopic and its notes, and verse numbering follows his. The Ge‘ez *Egzi’abḥer* is rendered “the Lord”, and the divine name Yahweh is not supplied where the text has none. **About the book.** Jubilees, also called “The Little Genesis” (Leptogenesis), retells Genesis 1 through Exodus 12–14 as a revelation given to Moses on Mount Sinai by “the angel of the presence”, who reads from heavenly tablets. It was written in Hebrew in the 2nd century BC (probably between about 160 and 150 BC), and was well known at Qumran, where fragments of about fifteen copies were found. Only an Ethiopic translation, made from Greek, preserves the whole book; it is part of the Old Testament of the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church and the Eritrean Orthodox Church (as “Kufale”) and of the Scriptures of Beta Israel. Its patriarchs keep the Sabbath, the festivals, and the laws of Sinai before Sinai, and its main concern is to defend a solar calendar. **Dates in Jubilees.** The book reckons by a calendar of 364 days, which is 52 weeks exactly: four quarters of 13 weeks (91 days), each quarter having months of 30, 30, and 31 days, so that each festival falls on the same day of the week every year. The book teaches that the lunar calendars used in Jerusalem are a deadly error (6:32–38). Years are grouped in “weeks” of 7 years and “jubilees” of 7 weeks, 49 years, and an event is dated by year, week, and jubilee (for example, “the second year of the third week of the forty-fifth jubilee”). In this edition months and days are given by their number in the text, with modern equivalents in footnotes on the assumption that month 1, day 1 (a Wednesday) falls about March 22; so the Passover, month 1, day 14, is about April 4, the Feast of Weeks (month 3, day 15) about June 4, and the Day of Atonement (month 7, day 10) about September 29. Charles’s marginal “A.M.” (anno mundi) year numbers, which give each event’s year from creation, are cited in the notes as “in Charles’s count”; they are his calculation and are not printed in the text of the Ethiopic. A “week of years” in the notes means seven years, a “jubilee” forty-nine years. Measures are converted to modern US customary units, with the original and the metric figure in the notes (a cubit is taken as 18 inches). Verse numbering follows Charles; in a few chapters where the Ethiopic manuscripts, the Latin, and the Hebrew fragments differ, the notes say so.

verses.text: In the first year after the Israelites left Egypt, on the sixteenth day of the third month,{a} God said to Moses, “Come up to me on the mountain. I will give you the two stone tablets of the law and the commandment, which I have written so that you may teach them.”{b}
So Moses went up the mountain of God, and the glory of the Lord settled on Mount Sinai, and a cloud covered it for six days.
On the seventh day he called Moses out of the cloud, and the sight of the Lord’s glory on the mountaintop was like a blazing fire.
Moses stayed on the mountain forty days and forty nights, and God showed him the history of all the days of the law and the testimony, from the earliest times to the latest.{c}

He said, “Set your heart on every word I speak to you on this mountain, and write them in a book, so that their descendants may see that I never abandoned them, however much evil they did by breaking the covenant that I am making today between me and you on Mount Sinai, for all their generations.
When all these things have come upon them, they will recognize that I am more just than they in every judgment and in every act, and that I was truly with them.

You must write down for yourself all the words that I tell you today. I know how rebellious and stubborn they are, even before I bring them into the land that I promised on oath to their ancestors, to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob: ‘I will give your descendants a land flowing with milk and honey.’
They will eat and be full, and then turn to foreign gods, which cannot rescue them from any of their troubles; and this witness will be heard against them.

They will forget every commandment I give them, and follow the nations, their filth and their shamelessness, and serve their gods, and those gods will become a trap, a distress, an affliction, and a snare for them.

Many will be destroyed and carried off, and will fall into the hands of their enemies, because they abandoned my rules and my commandments, the festivals of my covenant, my sabbaths, my holy place that I made holy for myself among them, my tabernacle, and my sanctuary, which I made holy for myself in the middle of the land, so that I might set my name there and have it dwell.{d}

They will build themselves high places, sacred poles, and carved idols, and each will bow down to his own, and be led astray; they will sacrifice their children to demons and to every product of their hearts’ delusion.

I will send witnesses to them to testify against them, but they will not listen; they will kill the witnesses, and hunt down those who look for the law. They will do away with it all and twist it into something wicked in my sight.
Then I will hide my face from them and hand them over to the nations to be taken captive, plundered, and devoured. I will uproot them from the land and scatter them among the nations.
They will forget my whole law, all my commandments, and all my judgments, and lose their way over the new moons, sabbaths, festivals, jubilees, and ordinances.{e}

After that they will turn back to me from among the nations, with all their heart, all their soul, and all their strength. I will gather them from all the nations, and they will look for me, and I will let them find me when they look for me with all their heart and all their soul.

I will show them plentiful peace with justice, and I will plant them as a plant of uprightness, with all my heart and all my soul.{f} They will be a blessing and not a curse; they will be the head and not the tail.
I will build my sanctuary among them and live with them; I will be their God, and they will be my people in truth and righteousness.
I will not abandon them or let them down, for I am the Lord their God.”

Moses fell on his face and prayed: “Lord, my God, do not abandon your people and your inheritance, to wander in the delusions of their own hearts. Do not hand them over to their enemies, the nations, to rule over them and make them sin against you.

Lord, lift up your mercy over your people, and create in them an upright spirit. Do not let the spirit of Beliar rule them, accuse them before you, and trap them off every path of righteousness, so that they are destroyed from your presence.{g}

They are your people and your inheritance, whom you rescued with your great power from the Egyptians. Create in them a clean heart and a holy spirit, and never let them be trapped by their sins, from now on and forever.”
The Lord answered Moses: “I know how perverse they are, with their schemes and their stubbornness. They will not obey until they confess their own sin and the sin of their ancestors.

After that they will turn back to me in complete uprightness, with their whole heart and soul. I will cut away the foreskin of their hearts and of the hearts of their descendants, and create a holy spirit in them, and cleanse them so that they never again turn away from me, from that day on and forever.
Their souls will cling to me and to all my commandments, and they will keep them; I will be their Father, and they will be my children.
All of them will be called children of the living God, and every angel and every spirit will know that these are my children, that I am their Father in truth and justice, and that I love them.

Now write down for yourself all these words that I tell you on this mountain, the first and the last, everything that will happen in all the divisions of days, under the law and the testimony, in the weeks and the jubilees, forever, until I come down and live with them for all time.”
Then he said to the angel of the presence, “Write for Moses from the beginning of creation until my sanctuary is built among them for all eternity.{h}
The Lord will appear before the eyes of all, and all will know that I am the God of Israel, the Father of all Jacob’s children, and king on Mount Zion forever. Zion and Jerusalem will be holy.”{i}

Then the angel of the presence, who went ahead of Israel’s camp, took the tablets of the divisions of the years, from the time of creation, the law and the testimony of the weeks and the jubilees, year by year, in the full count of the jubilees, from the day of the new creation, when the heavens, the earth and all creation will be renewed according to the powers of heaven and all the works of the earth, until the Lord’s sanctuary is made in Jerusalem on Mount Zion, and all the lights are renewed for healing, peace, and blessing for all the chosen of Israel, so that it may be so from that day forever.{j}

notes.text: The sixteenth day of the third month: Ge‘ez gives only “the third month, the sixteenth day.” Jubilees counts months by number (as the older books of the Bible often do) in its fixed 364-day calendar, which begins at the spring equinox on a Wednesday (see the note at 6:29–32). In that calendar the sixteenth day of the third month falls in early June, a day after the Feast of Weeks that Jubilees fixes on the fifteenth (6:17–22). Compare Exod 19:1.

The Prologue, which Charles prints before 1:1 without a verse number, reads: “This is the account of the division of the days, of the law and the testimony, of the events of the years, of their weeks of years and their jubilees, through all the years of the world, as the Lord told Moses on Mount Sinai when he went up to receive the tablets of the law and the commandment, at God’s own word to him: ‘Go up to the top of the mountain.’” A week of years is seven years; a jubilee is seven such weeks, forty-nine years (compare Lev 25).

The earlier and the later history: the Ethiopic has “the first and the last,” which Charles takes to mean the whole sweep of history, from creation to the final age. The book presents itself as that revelation, dictated to Moses by an angel (1:27).
My holy place … my sanctuary: the Temple in Jerusalem. The writer speaks of the tabernacle as still standing in the time of the kings, and the “land” that holds the sanctuary is Judah.

Lose their way over the new moons: an early hint of the book’s main quarrel. Jubilees insists that the year has exactly 364 days, 52 weeks, with festivals on fixed dates, and rejects calendars governed by the moon (see 6:29–38).

I will plant them as a plant of uprightness: the Ethiopic text is damaged here (Charles marks it as corrupt). The sense given is his proposed restoration, “I will plant them … in the land,” following Jer 32:41.
Beliar: the Ethiopic form of Belial (“worthlessness”), here the chief of the evil spirits. He appears again in 1:20 and in Jubilees’ other mentions of demonic rule; compare Mastema (10:8).

The angel of the presence: the angel who stands before God’s face (Isa 63:9). Later (2:1) he dictates the account to Moses, and Jubilees is presented as his words. Charles suggested Michael. The idea that the law came through angels is also found in Gal 3:19.
This verse stands here in the manuscripts, but Charles thought it belongs after verse 25.
Charles considered the middle of this sentence damaged in the Ethiopic. The “new creation” looks ahead to the end of days (compare Isa 65:17; Rev 21:1).

chapters.heading: God’s Words to Moses on Mount Sinai

verses.text: The angel of the presence spoke to Moses at the Lord’s word: “Write the full story of creation: how the Lord God finished all his work and everything he made in six days, rested on the seventh day, made it holy for all ages, and set it as a sign for all his works.

On the first day he made the heavens above, the earth, the waters, and all the spirits that serve before him: the angels of the presence, the angels of holiness, the angels of the spirits of fire, of the winds, of the clouds, of darkness, of snow, hail and frost, the angels of the voices, of thunder and lightning, the angels of the spirits of cold and heat, winter and spring, autumn and summer, and of every spirit of his creatures in heaven and on earth. He also made the depths and the darkness, evening and night, and the light, dawn and day, which he prepared in the knowledge of his heart.{a}
Then we saw his works and praised him and sang before him for all that he had made, for he made seven great works on the first day.

On the second day he made the firmament in the midst of the waters, and the waters were divided that day: half rose above it and half sank below it, over the surface of the whole earth. This was the only work he made on the second day.
On the third day he commanded the waters to withdraw from the surface of the whole earth into one place, and the dry ground to appear.
The waters obeyed him, pulling back from the face of the earth into one place beyond this firmament, and the dry ground appeared.

That day he made for them all the seas, each in its basin, all the rivers, the pools of water in the hills and across the earth, all the lakes, all the dew on the ground, and the seed that is sown, all that sprouts, the fruit trees, the trees of the forest, and the garden of Eden in Eden, and every plant of every kind. These four great works God made on the third day.{b}
On the fourth day he made the sun, the moon, and the stars, and set them in the sky’s firmament to give light over the whole earth, to rule the day and the night, and to separate light from darkness.
God set the sun as a great sign on the earth, for days, sabbaths, months, festivals, years, sabbaths of years, jubilees, and every season of the years.{c}
It separates light from darkness and brings prosperity, so that everything that grows and sprouts on the earth may thrive. These three things he made on the fourth day.

On the fifth day he made the great sea creatures in the depths of the waters; these were the first flesh made by his hands. He made the fish and everything that moves in the water, and everything that flies, the birds and all their kinds.
The sun rose over them to make them thrive, and over everything on the earth, everything that sprouts from the ground, all the fruit trees, and all flesh. These three kinds he made on the fifth day.
On the sixth day he made all the wild animals of the earth, all the livestock, and everything that moves on the ground.

After all that, he made humankind, male and female, and gave them rule over everything on the earth and in the seas, over everything that flies, over the wild animals, the livestock, and everything that moves on the ground, over the whole earth; over all of this he gave them rule. These four kinds he made on the sixth day.
In all there were twenty-two kinds of things.{d}
He finished all his work on the sixth day: everything in the heavens and on the earth, in the seas and in the depths, in light and in darkness, and in everything.
He gave us a great sign, the sabbath day, so that we would work six days and keep sabbath on the seventh from all work.
All the angels of the presence and all the angels of holiness, these two great orders, he commanded to keep sabbath with him in heaven and on earth.

He said to us, ‘I will set apart a people for myself from all the peoples, and they will keep the sabbath. I will make them holy as my own people and bless them. Just as I have made the sabbath day holy, and still do, so I will bless them, and they will be my people and I will be their God.

I have chosen the descendants of Jacob out of everything I have seen and I have written him down as my firstborn son. I have made him holy for myself forever, and I will teach them the sabbath day, so that they may rest on it from all work.’

So he made in it a sign, so that they would keep sabbath with us on the seventh day, to eat and drink and bless the one who made all things, who has blessed and made holy for himself a special people above all peoples, and so that they would keep sabbath along with us.
He made their commands rise to him like a sweet fragrance, welcome to him every day.

There were twenty-two heads of the human race from Adam to Jacob, and twenty-two kinds of work were done until the seventh day. This seventh day is blessed and holy, and the other one is blessed and holy too; the one serves with the other for holiness and blessing.{e}
It was granted that Jacob and his descendants should always be the blessed and holy ones of the first testimony and law, just as he made the sabbath day holy and blessed on the seventh day.

He made heaven and earth and all that he made in six days, and God made the seventh day holy, because of all his works. So he commanded that anyone who does any work on it must die, and anyone who profanes it must surely die.{f}
So command the Israelites to keep this day and make it holy, to do no work on it and not to defile it, for it is holier than all other days.

Anyone who profanes it must certainly die, and anyone who does any work on it will die forever, so that the Israelites keep this day through all their generations and are not rooted out of the land. It is a holy day and a blessed day.
Everyone who keeps it, and rests on it from all his work, will be holy and blessed always, like us.

Tell the Israelites the law of this day: that they should keep sabbath on it and not abandon it in the delusions of their hearts; that it is not allowed to do on it anything inappropriate or to pursue their own pleasure; that they should not prepare anything to eat or drink on it, nor draw water, nor carry any load in or out through their gates that they did not prepare for themselves at home on the sixth day.{g}

They must not bring anything in or out from house to house on that day, for that day is holier and more blessed than any jubilee day in the jubilees. On it we kept sabbath in heaven before it was made known to any human being that they should keep sabbath on the earth.

The Creator of all things blessed it, but he did not make all peoples and nations holy to keep the sabbath on it; only Israel. Only to them did he grant eating, drinking, and keeping sabbath on the earth.
The Creator of all things blessed this day that he had made, for a blessing, for holiness, and for glory above all days.
This law and testimony was given to the Israelites as an everlasting law throughout their generations.

notes.text: Seven works on the first day: heaven, earth, waters, spirits, the abysses, darkness, and light (verse 3 speaks of seven). The angels, in this book, are made on the first day, so they could not have helped with later work; later Jewish tradition disputed this. The two highest orders are “angels of the presence” and “angels of holiness.” The rest are the angels who govern natural forces; compare 1 Enoch 60:11–21 and 75:3.
Four works on the third day: Genesis names three (dry land and seas, plants, fruit trees); Jubilees adds the garden of Eden.

The sun, and not the moon, is the sign. This is the book’s central calendar claim: it follows the sun’s fixed year of 364 days (52 weeks), and the moon plays no part in its reckoning (compare 6:36–38).

Twenty-two: seven on day one, one on day two, four on day three, three on day four, three on day five, four on day six. The number matches the letters of the Hebrew alphabet, the twenty-two books (of the Hebrew Bible, as counted), and the twenty-two generations from Adam to Jacob (verse 23).

Between verses 22 and 23 Charles marks a gap in the Ethiopic and proposes this restoration: “As there are twenty-two letters, and twenty-two sacred books, and twenty-two heads of humankind from Adam to Jacob, so there were twenty-two kinds of work.” “The other one” in the second half of this verse is Jacob (Israel).
Compare Exod 31:14–15 and Num 15:32–36.
Charles considered part of this verse out of order in the Ethiopic. The ban on carrying burdens recalls Jer 17:21–22. Anything to eat was to be prepared the day before (Exod 16:23).

chapters.heading: The Creation and the Sabbath

verses.text: During the six days of the second week, at God’s word, we brought to Adam all the wild animals, livestock, birds, and everything that moves on the ground or in the water, each by kind and species: the wild animals on the first day, the livestock on the second, the birds on the third, everything that moves on the ground on the fourth, and what moves in the water on the fifth.{a}
Adam gave names to them all, and whatever he called each one became its name.
For those five days Adam watched all of them, male and female, of every kind on earth, but he was alone, and found no companion suitable for him.
Then the Lord said to us, “It is not good for the man to be alone. Let us make a helper for him.”
The Lord our God sent a deep sleep upon him, and he slept. God took one of his ribs to make the woman; this rib was the beginning of the woman. He built up flesh in its place and formed the woman.

Then he roused Adam from his sleep, and as soon as Adam woke he rose to his feet; it was the sixth day. The Lord led the woman to him, and Adam recognized her and said, “At last: bone from my bones, flesh from my flesh! She shall be called my wife, since she was drawn out of her husband.”
This is why a man and wife become one, and why a man leaves his father and mother and clings to his wife, and the two become one flesh.

Adam was made in the first week, and the rib, his wife, in the same week; in the second week God showed her to him. For this reason the commandment was given to keep the days of uncleanness: seven days for a male child, and twice seven for a female.{b}

When Adam had completed forty days in the land where he was made, we brought him into the garden of Eden to work it and take care of it, but his wife was brought in on the eightieth day, and only after that did she enter the garden of Eden.

This is why the commandment about a woman giving birth is written on the heavenly tablets: “If she gives birth to a boy, she is unclean for seven days, as in the first week of days, and then thirty-three days she must remain in the blood of her purifying. She must touch nothing holy and must not enter the sanctuary until she has completed the days set for a male child.{c}
But for a girl she is unclean for two weeks of days, as in the first two weeks, and sixty-six days in the blood of purifying, eighty days in all.”
When she had completed eighty days, we brought her into the garden of Eden, because it is holier than all the rest of the earth, and every tree planted in it is holy.
So the rule for a woman who bears a boy or a girl is these days: she must touch nothing holy and not enter the sanctuary until those days for a boy or a girl are complete.
This is the law and testimony written for Israel, so that they will keep it always.
In the first week of the first jubilee, Adam and his wife lived in the garden of Eden for seven years, working and tending it; we gave him tasks and taught him everything fit for farming.{d}

He worked the garden, and was naked and did not know it, and was not ashamed. He guarded the garden from the birds, wild animals, and livestock, gathered its fruit and ate it, and put aside the rest for himself and his wife.
When the seven years were complete, in the second month, on the seventeenth day, the serpent came to the woman and said, “Did God tell you not to eat from every tree in the garden?”

She answered, “God told us we may eat the fruit of all the trees of the garden, but about the fruit of the tree in the middle of the garden, God said, ‘Do not eat it, and do not even touch it, or you will die.’”
The serpent said to the woman, “You certainly will not die. God knows that on the day you eat it, your eyes will be opened, you will be like gods, and you will know good and evil.”
The woman saw that the tree was pleasant and lovely to look at, and that its fruit was good to eat, and she took some and ate.
She first covered her shame with fig leaves, then gave some to Adam, and he ate; his eyes were opened, and he saw that he was naked.
He took fig leaves and sewed them together, made himself an apron, and covered his shame.
God cursed the serpent and was angry with it forever.{e}

He was angry with the woman, because she had listened to the serpent’s voice and eaten. He said to her, “I will greatly increase your sorrow and pain; you will bear children in sorrow, and you will turn back to your husband, and he will rule over you.”{f}

To Adam he said, “Because you listened to your wife and ate from the tree I told you not to eat from, the ground is cursed because of you. It will produce thorns and thistles for you, and you will eat your bread by the sweat of your face, until you return to the earth you were taken from; you are earth, and to earth you will return.”
He made them coats of skin, dressed them, and sent them out of the garden of Eden.
On the day Adam left the garden, he offered a sweet-smelling offering of incense—frankincense, galbanum, stacte, and spices—in the morning when the sun rose, the day he had covered his shame.{g}

That day the mouths of all the wild animals, livestock, birds, and every creature that walks or moves were shut, so that they could no longer speak; until then they had all spoken to one another with one lip and one tongue.{h}
He sent out of the garden of Eden every creature that had been in it, and all were scattered by kind and species to the places made for them.
To Adam alone he gave the means to cover his shame, out of all the animals and livestock.
That is why the heavenly tablets prescribe that all who know the judgment of the law must cover their shame and not uncover themselves as the nations do.{i}
On the new moon of the fourth month Adam and his wife left the garden of Eden and settled in the land of Elda, the land of their creation.{j}
Adam named his wife Eve.
They had no son until the first jubilee, and after that he knew her.{k}
Adam worked the land as he had been taught in the garden of Eden.

notes.text: The “second week” is the second week of creation, counted from the first sabbath, which is the beginning of the first week of the world’s history. The “we” is the angels of the presence, who speak throughout this account.
Compare Lev 12:2–5. The writer explains the law of purification after childbirth from the order of events in Eden.

The heavenly tablets: tablets in heaven on which God has written law and the course of history. Jubilees often appeals to them for rules, including some not found in the Pentateuch (1 Enoch 81:1–2 and 93:2 also mention them).
Seven years: the first week of years. A tradition recorded in Jewish literature says that Adam was in Eden only a few hours; Jubilees makes it seven years.
Charles suspected something has dropped out here. He suggested it described the loss of the serpent’s legs, a tradition found in the Aramaic Targum on Genesis and in Josephus.
You will turn back to your husband: so the Greek and Syriac in Gen 3:16; the Hebrew has “your desire will be for your husband.”
Compare the incense of Exod 30:34. Adam is made the first priest.
Josephus also says that all creatures spoke in the garden. In Jubilees the single original language is Hebrew (12:25–26).
The nations … uncover themselves: likely a reference to Greek athletic exercise in the nude, which pious Jews of the second century BC opposed (1 Macc 1:14–15; 2 Macc 4:12–14).

The new moon of the fourth month: here “new moon” means the first day of the fourth month (about June 21, the summer solstice, in the 364-day calendar of Jubilees). Elda: perhaps a form of the Hebrew word for “birth.” Charles thought so.
Eve: Hebrew Ḥawwah, associated with “living” in Gen 3:20.

chapters.heading: Eden and the Fall

verses.text: In the third week of the second jubilee Eve gave birth to Cain, in the fourth week to Abel, and in the fifth week to her daughter Awan.{a}
In the first year of the third jubilee, Cain killed Abel, because God accepted Abel’s sacrifice and refused Cain’s offering.
He killed him in the field, and his blood cried out from the ground to heaven, accusing him of the murder.
The Lord rebuked Cain for killing Abel, made him a wanderer on the earth because of his brother’s blood, and cursed him on the earth.

For that reason it is written on the heavenly tablets: “Cursed is the one who strikes his neighbor in secret. Let everyone who has seen and heard say, ‘So be it.’ And cursed too is the one who saw and did not report it.”{b}
That is why, when we appear before the Lord our God, we report all the sin that is committed in heaven and on earth, in light and in darkness, and everywhere.

Adam and his wife grieved over Abel for four weeks of years. In the fourth year of the fifth week they were glad again, and Adam knew his wife, and she bore a son. He named him Seth, saying, “God has raised up a second child for us on the earth in place of Abel, because Cain killed him.”{c}
In the sixth week he fathered his daughter Azura.

Cain took his sister Awan as his wife, and at the end of the fourth jubilee she bore him Enoch. In the first year of the first week of the fifth jubilee, houses were built on the earth, and Cain built a city and named it after his son Enoch.{d}
Adam knew Eve his wife, and she bore nine more sons.
In the fifth week of the fifth jubilee Seth took his sister Azura as his wife, and in the fourth year of the sixth week she bore him Enos.
He was the first to call on the name of the Lord on the earth.
In the third week of the seventh jubilee Enos took his sister Noam as his wife, and in the third year of the fifth week she bore him a son, whom he named Kenan.
At the end of the eighth jubilee Kenan took his sister Mualeleth as his wife, and in the first week of the ninth jubilee, in the third year, she bore him a son, whom he named Mahalalel.{e}

In the second week of the tenth jubilee Mahalalel took Dinah, daughter of Barakiel, his father’s brother’s daughter, as his wife, and in the third week, in the sixth year, she bore him a son, whom he named Jared, because in his days the angels of the Lord came down to earth.{f} They are called the Watchers, and were sent to teach people, and to practice justice and uprightness on earth.

In the eleventh jubilee, during its fourth week, Jared married Baraka, the daughter of Rasuel, who was his cousin on his father’s side. In the fifth week, in the jubilee’s fourth year, she bore him a son, whom he called Enoch.

Enoch was the first person born on earth to learn writing, knowledge, and wisdom, and he wrote the signs of the sky in a book, in the order of their months, so that people might know the seasons of the years in the order of their months.{g}

He was the first to write a testimony, and he testified to the human race in the generations of the earth. He set out the weeks of the jubilees, made known the days of the years, arranged the months, and counted the sabbaths of years, as we had shown him.

He saw in a dream-vision what has been and what will be, how it will go for human beings in all their generations until the day of judgment. He saw and understood everything, wrote down his testimony, and placed it on earth for all human beings and their generations.

In the twelfth jubilee, in the seventh week, he took a wife named Edni, daughter of Danel, his father’s brother’s daughter, and in the sixth year of that week she bore him a son, whom he named Methuselah.
He then spent six jubilees of years with God’s angels, who showed him everything on earth and in heaven, the course of the sun, and he wrote it all down.
He warned the Watchers who had sinned with the daughters of men; they had begun to join themselves to them and to be defiled, and Enoch bore witness against all of them.

He was taken from among human beings, and we led him into the garden of Eden in majesty and honor, and there he writes down the condemnation and judgment of the world and all the wickedness of humankind.{h}

Because of that, God brought the waters of the flood over all the land of Eden, for he was put there as a sign, to testify against all human beings and recount every deed of every generation until the day of judgment.
He burned the incense of the sanctuary, sweet-smelling spices, welcome to the Lord on the mountain.

For the Lord has four places on earth: the garden of Eden, the mountain of the east, this mountain where you are today, Mount Sinai, and Mount Zion, which will be made holy in the new creation to make the earth holy; through it the earth will be cleansed of all its guilt and uncleanness in all the generations of the world.{i}

In the fourteenth jubilee Methuselah took a wife, Edna, daughter of Azriel, his father’s brother’s daughter, in the third week, in the first year of that week, and he fathered a son and named him Lamech.

In the fifteenth jubilee, in the third week, Lamech took a wife named Betenos, daughter of Barakiel, his father’s brother’s daughter, and in that week she bore him a son. He named him Noah, saying, “This one will comfort me in my trouble and all my work, and over the ground that the Lord cursed.”{j}
At the end of the nineteenth jubilee, in the seventh week, in its sixth year, Adam died, and all his sons buried him in the land of his creation. He was the first to be buried in the earth.

He was seventy years short of a thousand years, for a thousand years are like one day in the testimony of heaven, and so it was written about the tree of knowledge: “On the day you eat from it you will die.” For that reason he did not complete the years of that day; he died during it.{k}

At the end of that jubilee, in the same year, Cain was killed after him; his house fell on him, and he died in the middle of it, killed by its stones. He had killed Abel with a stone, and a stone killed him, a just judgment.
For that reason it was ordained on the heavenly tablets: “With the tool a man uses to kill his neighbor, he is to be killed; as he wounded him, so they are to treat him.”{l}

In the twenty-fifth jubilee Noah took a wife named Emzara, daughter of Rakeel, his father’s brother’s daughter, in the first year of the fifth week. In the third year of it she bore him Shem, in the fifth year Ham, and in the first year of the sixth week Japheth.

notes.text: Jubilees fills in what Genesis leaves out, including the wives of the early patriarchs, who are all sisters or cousins. Awan: “iniquity” (Hebrew ’awen). Cain’s wife is his sister in this book, as in later Jewish tradition.
Compare Deut 27:24.
Seth: in Gen 4:25 Eve explains the name as “God has appointed (shath) another child.” In Jubilees the father usually names the child.

Years in this book can be counted from creation: the first year of the first week of the fifth jubilee is year 197 (4 × 49 + 1). Charles gives these year numbers in his margins; they follow the book’s own chronology, in which a jubilee is forty-nine years.
Mualeleth: perhaps “she who praises God.”
Jared: the name suggests the Hebrew verb yarad, “come down.” The angels who came down are the Watchers, described in 1 Enoch 6.
Enoch writes the signs of the sky: compare the Astronomical Book (1 Enoch 72–82), which also lays out a 364-day solar year. Jubilees claims for the calendar the authority of the first scribe.
Taken from among human beings: Gen 5:24. Here he is in Eden as a heavenly scribe, as in 1 Enoch 12:3–4.

Four places: three of them are tied to a great figure—Eden to Adam, Sinai to Moses, Zion to David. The “mountain of the east” is uncertain; Charles allowed that it may be the mountain above Eden where Seth’s family lived.
Noah: Hebrew Noaḥ, tied to “comfort” (naḥam) in Gen 5:29.
A thousand years are like one day: compare Ps 90:4 and 2 Pet 3:8. Adam lived 930 years (Gen 5:5); Jubilees says 930, “seventy short of a thousand.”
The law of equal retribution: compare Exod 21:24; Lev 24:19–20.

chapters.heading: Cain and Abel; the Line to Noah

verses.text: When human beings began to multiply across the earth and daughters were born to them, the angels of God saw them in a certain year of this jubilee, saw that they were beautiful, and took wives for themselves from any they chose. They bore sons to them, and these were giants.{a}

Lawlessness grew on the earth, and all flesh corrupted its way: human beings, livestock, wild animals, birds, and everything that walks on the earth all corrupted their ways and their natures. They began to devour one another, lawlessness grew on the earth, and every thought of every human heart was evil continually.
God looked at the earth, and it was corrupt: all flesh had corrupted its natural order, and everything on the earth had done every kind of evil before his eyes.
He said, “I will destroy people and all flesh on the face of the earth, which I made.”
But Noah found favor in the Lord’s eyes.

He was furious with the angels whom he had sent to earth, and commanded that they be uprooted from all their power. He told us to bind them in the depths of the earth, and there they are, bound in the midst of it, and kept apart.
Against their sons a command went out from before his face: that they be struck down with the sword and removed from under heaven.
He said, “My spirit will not remain in human beings forever, for they too are flesh, and their days will be a hundred and twenty years.”{b}
He sent his sword among them so that each killed his neighbor, and they began to kill each other until all had fallen by the sword and been wiped from the earth.

Their fathers saw their destruction, and afterward were bound in the depths of the earth forever, until the day of the great condemnation, when judgment will be carried out on all who have corrupted their ways and works before the Lord.{c}
He destroyed all of them from their places, and not one remained whom he did not judge according to all their wickedness.
He made a new and righteous nature for all his works, so that they would not sin in their whole nature forever, but all be righteous, each according to its kind, always.

The judgment of all is ordained and written on the heavenly tablets in justice, even the judgment of all who leave the path set for them to walk. If they do not walk in it, judgment is written for every creature and for every kind.
There is nothing in heaven or on earth, in light or in darkness, in Sheol or in the deep, or in the place of darkness, that is not judged; all their judgments are ordained, written, and engraved.
He will judge all of them, the great according to their greatness and the small according to their smallness, each according to his path.

He does not show partiality, nor does he accept bribes. If he says he will judge each one, then even if someone gave everything on earth, he would not accept the gifts or the person, and would take nothing from his hand, for he is a righteous judge.
The decree written down for the Israelites is this: if they come back to him in justice, he will forgive every offense and overlook every sin.
The decree is written that he will have compassion on all who repent of their guilt, one day in each year.{d}

As for all who corrupted their ways and thoughts before the flood, no one’s person was accepted except Noah’s; for his sake his sons were accepted, and God saved them from the waters of the flood on his account, because his heart was righteous in all his ways, as had been commanded concerning him, and he had not departed from anything ordained for him.
The Lord said he would destroy everything on the earth, people, livestock, wild animals, birds of the air, and everything that moves on the ground.
He commanded Noah to build an ark so that he could be saved from the waters of the flood.
Noah built the ark exactly as he was commanded, in the twenty-seventh jubilee of years, in the fifth week, in the fifth year, on the first day of the first month.{e}

In the sixth year of it, in the second month, on the first day of the second month, he entered, along with everything we brought to him, into the ark, and on the seventeenth, in the evening, the Lord shut it from outside.{f}
The Lord opened seven floodgates of heaven and the mouths of the springs of the great deep, seven mouths in number.{g}
The floodgates began to pour water from the sky for forty days and forty nights, and the springs of the deep also sent up water, until the whole world was full of water.
The waters rose on the earth: fifteen cubits above all the high mountains.{h} The ark rose above the ground and moved across the surface of the waters.
The water covered the earth for five months, a hundred and fifty days.
The ark came to rest on the top of Lubar, one of the mountains of Ararat.{i}

When the fourth month began, the fountains of the great deep were sealed and the windows of heaven were shut. When the seventh month began, every opening in the earth’s depths was uncovered, and the water started to sink away into the deep below.
On the first day of the tenth month the mountaintops were seen, and on the first day of the first month the earth was visible.
The waters disappeared from the earth in the fifth week, in its seventh year, and on the seventeenth day of the second month the earth was dry.
On the twenty-seventh day of it he opened the ark and sent out the wild animals, livestock, birds, and every moving thing.{j}

notes.text: Angels of God: the Hebrew of Gen 6:2 has “sons of God.” Jubilees follows the older reading of the Greek version, “angels,” and so does 1 Enoch (chapters 6–7). Giants: Hebrew Nephilim.
Compare Gen 6:3.

Charles argued that verses 10–12 describe the final judgment, so that “were bound” should be read “are bound” and the verbs in verse 11 are future: “He will destroy all from their places and not one will be left whom he does not judge.” This translation keeps the Ethiopic tenses, which treat it as already happened.

Verses 17–18 look like a later addition borrowed from 34:18–19. The reference is to the Day of Atonement, on the tenth day of the seventh month (about October 1 in the 364-day calendar; see 34:18–19).
The twenty-seventh jubilee, fifth week, fifth year is year 1307 from creation (26 × 49 + 28 + 5). The first day of the first month is the first Wednesday of the year, in late March.

On the first day of the second month: about April 21. The seventeenth of the second month: about May 7. The year in the 364-day calendar starts on a Wednesday at about the spring equinox. The seventeenth of the second month is Gen 7:11.
Seven: in this book the number seven recurs in many places connected with the flood, as with the weeks and the jubilees.
Fifteen cubits: about 22 feet (a cubit being about 18 inches, or 45 centimeters; about 6.7 meters). Compare Gen 7:20.
Lubar: a mountain name found only in this book (see 7:1 and 7:17).

Charles notes that Gen 8:14 gives the twenty-seventh day of the second month as the day the earth was dry; here the earth dries on the seventeenth and the ark is opened ten days later. The year of the flood, in all, runs from the second month (about April 21) through a year to the second month of the next year, a full 364-day year and ten days.

chapters.heading: The Watchers, the Giants, and the Flood

verses.text: On the first day of the third month he came out of the ark and built an altar on that mountain.{a}
He made atonement for the earth, and took a kid and made atonement with its blood for all the guilt of the earth, for everything that had been on it was destroyed, except those in the ark with Noah.

He put the fat of it on the altar. He took an ox, a goat, a sheep, kids, salt, a turtledove, and a young pigeon, and laid a burnt offering on the altar; he poured out on it a grain offering mixed with oil, sprinkled wine, and strewed frankincense over everything, and sent up a pleasing fragrance, welcome to the Lord.

The Lord smelled the pleasing fragrance, and made a covenant with him that there would never again be a flood to destroy the earth, that seedtime and harvest would never cease in all the days of the earth, and that cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night would never change their order or end.
“As for you, be fruitful and multiply on the earth, and become many on it, and be a blessing on it. I will put fear and dread of you in everything that lives on the earth and in the sea.

I have given you all the wild animals, all the winged creatures, everything that moves on the ground, and the fish in the waters, and everything, for food; as with the green plants, I have given you everything to eat.

But you must not eat flesh with its life, that is, with the blood. The life of all flesh is in the blood, or else your own blood, your lives, will be demanded. From the hand of every man and from the hand of every animal I will demand the blood of a human being.
Whoever sheds a man’s blood, by a man his own blood will be shed, for God made humankind in his own image.
As for you, be fruitful and multiply on the earth.”
Noah and his sons swore that they would not eat any blood that was in any flesh, and he made a covenant before the Lord God forever, throughout all the generations of the earth, in this month.{b}

For that reason he told you to make a covenant with the Israelites in this month, on the mountain, with an oath, and to sprinkle blood on them over all the words of the covenant that the Lord made with them forever.{c}

This testimony is written about you, that you must always keep it, and never eat the blood of any animal, bird, or livestock, on any day, in all the days of the earth. Anyone who eats the blood of an animal, livestock, or bird, in all the days of the earth, he and his descendants will be rooted out of the land.
Command the Israelites to eat no blood, so that their names and their descendants will always be before the Lord our God.

There is no limit of days for this law, for it is forever. They must keep it through their generations, so that they may keep making supplication for you with blood before the altar. Every day, morning and evening, they must seek forgiveness on your behalf continually before the Lord, so that they keep the covenant and are not rooted out.{d}
He gave Noah and his sons a sign that there would never again be a flood on the earth.
He set his bow in the cloud as a sign of the everlasting covenant, that there would never again be a flood to destroy the earth all the days of the earth.
For that reason it is ordained and written on the heavenly tablets that they celebrate the Feast of Weeks in this month, once a year, to renew the covenant every year.{e}

This whole festival was kept in heaven from the day of creation until the days of Noah: twenty-six jubilees and five weeks of years. Noah and his sons kept it for seven jubilees and one week of years, until the day Noah died. From that day his sons let it lapse until the days of Abraham, and they ate blood.
But Abraham kept it, and Isaac and Jacob and his children kept it, up to your time. In your time the Israelites forgot it, until you celebrated it again on this mountain.
Command the Israelites to keep this festival through all their generations as a commandment for them: on one day in the year, in this month, they are to celebrate the festival.
This is the Feast of Weeks, also called the Feast of First Fruits, a feast with two aspects and two purposes. Keep it as it is written and carved concerning it.{f}

For I wrote in the book of the first law, the one I wrote for you, that you should celebrate it at its season, on one day in the year, and I explained its sacrifices to you, so that the Israelites would remember and celebrate it through their generations in this month, one day each year.{g}

On the first day of the first month, the first day of the fourth month, the first day of the seventh month, and the first day of the tenth month are days of remembrance and days of the seasons in the four divisions of the year. They are written and ordained as a testimony forever.{h}
Noah established them for himself as festivals for all generations forever, so that they became a memorial to him.
On the first day of the first month he was told to make the ark, and on that day the earth became dry and he opened it and saw the earth.

On the first of the fourth month the openings of the lower abysses were stopped up. On the first of the seventh month every vent in the earth’s depths was uncovered, and the waters began pouring down into them.
On the first day of the tenth month the tops of the mountains were seen, and Noah was glad.
For that reason he established them for himself as festivals, as a lasting memorial, and so they are ordained.

They set them down on the heavenly tablets: each season has thirteen weeks, and from one memorial to the next passes thirteen weeks, from the first to the second, the second to the third, and the third to the fourth.{i}
All the days of the commandment are fifty-two weeks of days, and these make the whole year complete.
So it is engraved and ordained on the heavenly tablets, and there is no neglecting this commandment for a single year or from year to year.

Command the Israelites to keep the years by this count: three hundred and sixty-four days, and these make a complete year. They must not alter its time from its days or its festivals, for everything will fall out in them according to the testimony. They must not leave out a single day or disturb any festival.{j}
But if they neglect them and do not keep them as he commanded, they will disturb all their seasons, and the years will be shifted out of this order, and they will neglect their ordinances.
The Israelites will all forget. They will lose the track of the years, overlook the new moons, seasons, and sabbaths, and wander from the whole order of the year.{k}

For I know, and from now on I will tell you, and it is not of my own devising; the book lies written before me, and the division of days is ordained on the heavenly tablets, so that they will not forget the festivals of the covenant and walk by the festivals of the nations, in their error and ignorance.
For there will be those who watch the moon carefully; it throws the seasons out of order, and each year it comes ten days early.{l}

A time will come when they overturn the order, treating a detestable day as the day of witness and an impure day as a feast. They will mix up all the days, holy ones with impure and impure with holy, and make errors about months, sabbaths, festivals, and jubilees.

For that reason I am commanding you and testifying to you, so that you may testify to them: after your death your descendants will disturb it, so that they will not make the year only three hundred and sixty-four days. For that reason they will go wrong about the beginnings of the months, the seasons, the sabbaths, and the festivals, and they will eat all kinds of blood with all kinds of flesh.

notes.text: That mountain: Lubar (5:28).
In this month: the third month. The covenant with Noah, in this book, is renewed each year on the Feast of Weeks (verses 17–22).
He told you: God is speaking to Moses through the angel. The sprinkling of blood is from Exod 24:8.
This refers to the daily offering (Num 28:3–8). Charles noted that these verses carry the covenant with Noah over to Moses’ time, and verse 15 returns to Noah.

The Feast of Weeks (Hebrew Shavuot, later “Pentecost”) comes fifty days after the offering of the first sheaf. In this book it is celebrated on the fifteenth day of the third month, and it is tied to Noah’s covenant. Later Judaism associated it with the giving of the law on Sinai.
A double nature: it commemorates the covenant with Noah and also marks the first fruits of the wheat harvest.

The book of the first law is the Pentateuch, written by the angel. “One day” may also be read “the first day,” meaning the first day of the week, Sunday; the Feast of Weeks then always falls on a Sunday in this calendar. This is also the view of the Sadducees.

Days of remembrance: four days that begin the four quarters of the year (about March 22, June 21, September 20, and December 20). They correspond to the four “days that are not counted in the reckoning of the year” in 1 Enoch 75:1.

This is the heart of the book’s calendar. A year of 364 days is exactly 52 weeks, divided into four seasons of thirteen weeks (91 days: months of 30, 30, and 31 days). Because 364 is divisible by seven, each date falls on the same weekday every year. The year begins on a Wednesday, the fourth day of the week, when the sun and moon were made (2:8). Passover, the fourteenth of the first month, is always a Tuesday, the Feast of Weeks the fifteenth of the third month always a Sunday, and so on. The calendar is purely solar. It is also the calendar of 1 Enoch 72–82 and of many Dead Sea Scrolls, and it is one reason scholars link the book to the sect that kept the scrolls.

Charles saw a difficulty: 52 weeks do not divide into twelve months of 30 days. The solution is in the four extra days that fall at the end of each quarter (months of 30, 30, and 31 days), the “days of remembrance” of verse 23.
Compare 1 Enoch 82:4–6.
Ten days early: a year of twelve lunar months has about 354 days, ten or eleven fewer than the 364-day year.

chapters.heading: Noah’s Covenant, the Feast of Weeks, and the Year of 364 Days

verses.text: In the seventh week, in its first year, in this jubilee, Noah planted vines on the mountain where the ark had come to rest, called Lubar, one of the Ararat mountains. They bore fruit in the fourth year, and he guarded the fruit and gathered it that year, in the seventh month.{a}
He made wine from it and put it in a jar and kept it until the fifth year, until the first day of the first month.

He celebrated the day of this feast with joy. He offered a burnt offering to the Lord: a young ox, a ram, seven sheep a year old, and a kid of the goats, to make atonement for himself and his sons.{b}

He prepared the kid first and put some of its blood on the flesh that was on the altar he had made, and he laid all the fat on the altar where he made the burnt offering, and the ox, the ram, and the sheep, with all their flesh.

He put all their grain offerings mixed with oil on it, and then sprinkled wine on the fire he had earlier lit on the altar, and he placed incense on the altar, and sent up a sweet fragrance, welcome to the Lord his God.
He rejoiced and drank some of this wine, he and his children, with joy.
In the evening he went into his tent, and being drunk he lay down and slept, and lay uncovered in his tent as he slept.
Ham saw his father Noah naked, and went out and told his two brothers outside.
Shem took a garment and got up, he and Japheth, and they put the garment on their shoulders and walked backward and covered their father’s nakedness, with their faces turned away.
Noah woke from his sleep and knew all that his younger son had done to him, and he cursed him and said, “Cursed be Canaan; he will be a slave to his brothers.”{c}
He blessed Shem, saying, “Blessed be the Lord, the God of Shem, and let Canaan be his slave.
May God enlarge Japheth, and may God live in the tent of Shem, and may Canaan be his slave.”
Ham knew that his father had cursed his youngest son, and he was upset that he had cursed his son, and he left his father, he and his sons with him: Cush, Mizraim, Put, and Canaan.
He built himself a city and named it after his wife, Neelatamauk.
Japheth saw it and was jealous of his brother, and he too built himself a city and named it after his wife, Adataneses.
Shem lived with his father Noah, and built a city near his father, on the mountain, and he too named it after his wife, Sedeqetelebab.{d}
These three cities lie near Mount Lubar: Sedeqetelebab facing the mountain on the east, Neelatamauk on the south, and Adataneses on the west.
These are the sons of Shem: Elam, Asshur, Arpachshad (born two years after the flood), Lud, and Aram.
These are the sons of Japheth: Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras. These are the sons of Noah.

In the twenty-eighth jubilee Noah began to teach his grandsons the ordinances and commandments, and all the judgments he knew. He urged his sons to practice righteousness, to cover the shame of their flesh, to bless their Creator, to honor father and mother, to love their neighbor, and to guard their souls from fornication, uncleanness, and all injustice.{e}

The flood came on the earth because of these three things: the fornication in which the Watchers, against the law of their ordinances, went chasing after the daughters of men, taking wives from any they chose, and began the uncleanness.

They fathered sons, the Naphidim, and these were all unlike each other, and devoured each other. The giants killed the Naphil, and the Naphil killed the Eljo, and the Eljo killed humankind, and one person killed another.{f}
Everyone sold himself to do wrong and shed much blood, and the earth was filled with injustice.

After this they sinned against the animals and birds and everything that moves or walks on the earth; much blood was shed on the earth, and every thought and desire of human beings was vanity and evil continually.
The Lord wiped out everything from the face of the earth, because of the wickedness of their deeds, and because of the blood they had shed in the midst of the earth.

“We were left, I and you, my sons, and everything that entered the ark with us. Now I see your works before me, and you are not walking in righteousness; you have begun to walk the path of destruction, and you are splitting from one another, jealous of one another, so that, my sons, you are not at peace, each with his brother.

For I see that the demons have begun to lead you and your children astray, and I fear for you that after my death you will shed human blood on the earth, and that you too will be wiped from the face of the earth.
Whoever sheds human blood and whoever eats the blood of any flesh will all be wiped from the earth.

No one will be left who eats blood or sheds human blood on the earth, and no descendant of his will be left living under heaven. They will go down to Sheol and into the place of condemnation, and they will all be swept into the darkness of the deep by a violent death.

No blood is to be seen on you, from all the blood there will be all the days that you kill any animal or livestock or anything that flies on the earth. Do a good deed for your souls by covering what has been shed on the surface of the earth.

Do not be like the person who eats with the blood; guard yourselves so that no one eats blood in your presence. Cover the blood, for so I have been commanded to testify to you and your children, along with all flesh.{g}
Do not let the soul be eaten with the flesh, so that your blood, which is your life, will not be demanded from the hand of any flesh that sheds it on the earth.
The earth will not be clean from the blood shed on it, except through the blood of the one who shed it; only then will the earth be purified through all its generations.

Now, my children, listen: practice justice and righteousness, so that you will be planted in righteousness across the whole earth, and your glory be lifted high before my God, who saved me from the waters of the flood.
You will go and build cities for yourselves and plant in them all the plants on the earth, and all the fruit trees as well.

For three years the fruit of anything that is eaten will not be gathered. In the fourth year its fruit will be counted as holy, and they will offer it, acceptable before the Most High God, who made heaven and earth and everything. Let them offer the first of the wine and oil in abundance as first fruits on the altar of the Lord, who receives it, and let the servants of the Lord’s house eat what is left before the altar that receives it.{h}
In the fifth year, make the release, so that you release it in justice and uprightness, and you will be righteous, and everything you plant will prosper.{i}
This is what Enoch, your father’s father, commanded his son Methuselah, and Methuselah his son Lamech, and Lamech commanded me everything his fathers had commanded him.

I too will give you a command, my sons, as Enoch commanded his son in the first jubilees: while he was still alive, in the seventh generation, he commanded and testified to his son and his grandsons until the day of his death.”

notes.text: Lubar: see the note at 5:28. Charles dates the planting at year 1317 from creation. A fruit tree’s first three years of fruit were not to be eaten (Lev 19:23–25).
The feast: the first day of the first month, the New Year in this calendar (about March 22). Compare Num 29:2.
Compare Gen 9:25. In Jubilees the curse falls on Canaan because Noah’s blessing had already been given to all three sons (Gen 9:1), and God had blessed Ham.
The names of these wives come only from Jubilees. Sedeqetelebab appears to mean “righteousness of heart” (Hebrew ṣedeq + lebab).

From here to the end of the chapter, Charles saw a piece of a lost “Book of Noah” (compare 10:1–15 and 1 Enoch 106:19–107:3). Later Jewish teaching ascribed seven commandments to the sons of Noah for all peoples.

Naphidim, Naphil, Eljo: three classes of offspring. The Ethiopic spellings of the three names reflect Hebrew Nephilim and, perhaps, Elyo, a class otherwise unknown; Charles thought the text damaged here.
Cover the blood: compare Lev 17:13. Jubilees traces the law of blood back to Noah, not Moses.
Servants of the house of the Lord: the priests. Later Jewish law has the owners eat the rest in Jerusalem.
The release: Charles read “in the seventh year let it rest.” The Ethiopic text of the verse is uncertain.

chapters.heading: Noah’s Vineyard and His Warnings

verses.text: In the twenty-ninth jubilee, in the first week, at its beginning, Arpachshad took a wife named Rasuya, daughter of Susan, daughter of Elam, and in the third year of that week she bore him a son, whom he named Kainam.{a}
The boy grew, and his father taught him to write, and he went off to look for a place where he could take a city for himself.

He found an inscription that people of earlier generations had carved on a rock, and read what was on it, and copied it. It led him into sin, for it held the teaching of the Watchers, by which they observed omens from the sun, moon, and stars, in all the signs of heaven.{b}
He wrote it down and said nothing about it, for he was afraid to speak to Noah about it, in case he be angry with him over it.

In the thirtieth jubilee, in the second week, in its first year, he took a wife named Melka, daughter of Madai, son of Japheth, and in the fourth year he fathered a son, whom he named Shelah, saying, “Truly I have been sent.”{c}
Shelah grew up and took a wife named Muak, daughter of Kesed, his father’s brother, in the thirty-first jubilee, in the fifth week, in its first year.
She bore him a son in its fifth year, and he named him Eber. Eber took a wife named Azurad, daughter of Nebrod, in the thirty-second jubilee, in the seventh week, in its third year.
In its sixth year she bore him a son, whom he named Peleg, because in the days when he was born Noah’s descendants began to divide the earth among themselves; for that reason he named him Peleg.{d}
They divided it among themselves in secret, and told Noah.

At the beginning of the thirty-third jubilee they divided the earth into three parts, for Shem, Ham, and Japheth, each according to his inheritance, in the first year of the first week, when one of us, who had been sent, was with them.

He called his sons, and they came to him, they and their children, and he divided the earth into the lots that his three sons would take as their possession. They reached out their hands and took the writing from the bosom of Noah, their father.

On the writing, the lot of Shem came out as the middle of the earth, which he and his sons would take as an inheritance for themselves through the generations forever. It runs from the middle of the mountain range of Rafa, from the mouth of the water of the river Tina, and its portion goes west through the middle of this river and extends until it reaches the water of the abysses, out of which this river flows and pours its waters into the sea of Meat, and the river flows into the great sea. Everything to the north is Japheth’s, and everything to the south belongs to Shem.{e}
It extends until it reaches Karaso; this is in the bosom of the tongue that looks south.
His portion runs along the great sea, in a straight line until it reaches the west of the tongue that looks south, for this sea is called the tongue of the Egyptian sea.

From there it turns to the south, to the mouth of the great sea on the shore of its waters, and runs west to Afra, until it reaches the waters of the river Gihon, and south of the waters of Gihon, to the banks of this river.{f}

It runs east until it reaches the garden of Eden, to the south of it, and from the east of the whole land of Eden and the whole east it turns to the east, and goes on until it reaches the east of the mountain named Rafa, and comes down to the bank of the mouth of the river Tina.
This portion came to Shem and his sons by lot, to possess forever, through his generations, forever.

Noah was glad that this portion fell to Shem and his sons, and he remembered everything he had said in prophecy, for he had said, “Blessed be the Lord, the God of Shem, and may the Lord live in the dwelling of Shem.”

He understood that Eden’s garden is the holiest place and the Lord’s dwelling, that Mount Sinai is the center of the wilderness, and that Mount Zion is the center, the navel, of the earth. These three were made as sacred places, each facing the others.
He blessed the God of gods, who had put the word of the Lord in his mouth, and he blessed the Lord forever.

He knew that a blessed portion and a blessing had come to Shem and his sons through all generations: the whole land of Eden, the whole land of the Red Sea, the whole land of the east, India, the Red Sea and its mountains, the whole land of Bashan, the whole land of Lebanon, the islands of Kaftur, all the mountains of Sanir and Amana, the mountains of Asshur in the north, all the land of Elam, Asshur, Babylon, Susa and Maidai, all the mountains of Ararat, and the whole region beyond the sea, beyond the mountains of Asshur in the north: a blessed and spacious land, and everything in it is very good.{g}

For Ham came out the second portion, beyond the Gihon toward the south, to the right of the garden, and it extends south to all the mountains of fire, and west to the sea of Atel, and west to the sea of Mauk, into which everything that is not destroyed goes down.{h}

It goes north to the borders of Gadir and along the coast of the sea to the waters of the great sea, until it nears the river Gihon, and follows the river Gihon until it reaches the right of the garden of Eden.{i}
This is the land that came to Ham as his portion, to hold forever for himself and his sons through their generations forever.
Japheth’s share was the third. It lay past the river Tina, north of where its waters empty out, and stretched northeast across all of Gog’s territory and every land east of it.
It runs north, to the mountains of Qelt in the north, and toward the sea of Mauk, and comes out east of Gadir as far as the region of the waters of the sea.{j}
It runs until it approaches the west of Fara, and returns toward Aferag, and runs east to the waters of the sea of Meat.
It runs to the region of the river Tina in a northeasterly direction, until it nears the boundary of its waters, toward the mountain Rafa, and turns north.

This is the land that came to Japheth and his sons as the portion of his inheritance, to possess for himself and his sons through their generations forever: five great islands and a great land in the north.
Cold is its climate, while Ham’s land is scorching; Shem’s land is neither scorching nor cold but blends the two.

notes.text: Kainam (Cainan): he appears in the Greek version of Gen 11:13 and in Luke 3:36, but not in the Hebrew text.
Josephus tells of knowledge of the stars carved on pillars by the sons of Seth. Here the knowledge is corrupt, since it comes from the Watchers. Compare 1 Enoch 8:3.
Shelah: the name sounds like Hebrew shalaḥ, “send.” Compare Gen 10:24.
Peleg: Hebrew “division”; compare Gen 10:25.

The geography of this chapter is that of a map: Rafa is probably the Rhipaean mountains (the Urals in ancient geography); Tina is the Tanais, the river Don; Meat is the Sea of Azov; Gihon is the Nile; the great sea is the Mediterranean. The scheme is of the Jewish map of the world, with Jerusalem as the “navel” of the earth (verse 19; compare Ezek 38:12 and 1 Enoch 26:1).
Afra: the Roman province of Africa, the north African coast around Carthage.
Kaftur: Caphtor, probably Crete. Sanir: Senir, the Hebrew name for Mount Hermon. Maidai: Media.

The mountains of fire: the volcanic peaks of the south. The sea of Atel is the Atlantic; the sea of Mauk is the great ocean river that was supposed to encircle the world. Charles suggested that the text may mean “into which everything that falls is destroyed.”
Gadir: Gades, modern Cádiz in Spain.
Qelt: the Celts.

chapters.heading: Kainam and the Division of the Earth

verses.text: Ham divided his portion among his sons. The first portion came out for Cush, to the east; west of him for Mizraim; west of him for Put; and west of that, along the sea, for Canaan.{a}

Shem also divided his portion among his sons. The first portion came out for Elam and his sons, east of the Tigris, until it reaches the east: the whole land of India, along the Red Sea on its coast, the waters of Dedan, all the mountains of Mebri and Ela, the whole land of Susa, and everything on the side of Pharnak, to the Red Sea and the river Tina.
For Asshur came out the second portion: the whole land of Asshur, Nineveh, and Shinar, as far as the border of India, and it climbs and skirts the river.

For Arpachshad came out the third portion: the whole land of the Chaldean region east of the Euphrates, bordering the Red Sea, and all the waters of the desert near the tongue of the sea that looks toward Egypt, all the land of Lebanon, Sanir, and Amana, to the border of the Euphrates.
For Aram came out the fourth portion: the whole land of Mesopotamia between the Tigris and the Euphrates, north of the Chaldeans, to the border of the mountains of Asshur and the land of Arara.
For Lud came out the fifth portion: the mountains of Asshur and everything belonging to them, until it reaches the Great Sea, and the east of Asshur, his brother.
Japheth also divided his inherited land among his sons.
The first portion came out for Gomer, east of the northern side as far as the river Tina; in the north, for Magog, came out all the inner parts of the north, until it reaches the sea of Meat.
For Madai came out, as his portion to possess, the land west of his two brothers, to the islands and to the coasts of the islands.
For Javan came out the fourth portion: every island and the islands toward the border of Lud.{b}

For Tubal came out the fifth portion, in the middle of the tongue of land that approaches the border of Lud’s portion, to the second tongue, to the region beyond the second tongue, up to the third tongue.{c}
For Meshech came out the sixth portion: the whole region beyond the third tongue, until it approaches the east of Gadir.

For Tiras came out the seventh portion: four great islands in the middle of the sea, which reach to Ham’s portion; and the islands of Kamaturi fell by lot to the sons of Arpachshad as his inheritance.{d}

So Noah’s sons divided it among their sons in the presence of Noah their father, and he bound them all with an oath, laying a curse on anyone who tried to seize a portion that had not fallen to him by lot.

They all said, “So be it, so be it,” for themselves and their sons forever, through their generations until the day of judgment, when the Lord God will judge them with sword and fire for all the unclean wickedness of their errors, with which they have filled the earth with transgression, uncleanness, fornication, and sin.

notes.text: Cush: Ethiopia. Mizraim: Egypt. Put: Libya.
Javan: Greece (Ionia).
The three tongues are probably the three great peninsulas of southern Europe: Thrace, Greece, and Italy.
The last clause looks like a later addition (Charles), since Arpachshad was a son of Shem.

chapters.heading: The Portions of Noah’s Grandsons

verses.text: In the third week of this jubilee, unclean demons began to lead astray Noah’s grandsons, and to make them go wrong and destroy them.{a}
Noah’s sons came to their father Noah and told him about the demons that were leading astray, blinding, and killing his grandsons.

He prayed before the Lord his God: “God of the spirits of all humanity, you have been merciful to me. You rescued me and my sons from the floodwaters and did not wipe me out as you did those headed for destruction. Your favor to me has been immense, and your compassion for my soul has been immense. Let your favor rest on my sons, and do not let wicked spirits govern them, or they will wipe them from the earth.
But bless me and my sons, so that we may multiply and fill the earth.

You know how your Watchers, the fathers of these spirits, acted in my day; and as for these spirits that are alive, lock them up and hold them fast in the place of condemnation, so that they do not bring destruction on the sons of your servant, my God; for these are malicious and were made to destroy.
Do not let them rule over the spirits of the living, for you alone can rule over them. Do not let them have power over the sons of the righteous from now on and forever.”
The Lord our God told us to bind them all.

Mastema, the chief of the spirits, came and said, “Lord, Creator, let some of them stay with me, to listen to my voice and do all that I tell them; for if some are not left to me, I will not be able to carry out my will against human beings. They are meant for corruption and for leading astray under my judgment, for the wickedness of humankind is great.”{b}
God said, “Let a tenth of them stay with him, and let nine parts go down into the place of condemnation.”{c}
He told one of us to teach Noah all their medicines, for he knew they would not walk uprightly or strive in righteousness.{d}
We did everything he said: we bound all the malicious evil spirits in the place of condemnation, and left a tenth of them to be subject to Satan on the earth.
We explained to Noah all the medicines for their diseases and for their deceptions, and how he could heal with the herbs of the earth.
Noah wrote everything down in a book as we instructed him, about every kind of medicine. So the evil spirits were kept from hurting Noah’s sons.
He gave all that he had written to Shem, his eldest son, for he loved him very much above all his sons.
Noah died and joined his ancestors, and was buried on Mount Lubar, in Ararat.
He completed nine hundred and fifty years of life: nineteen jubilees, two weeks of years, and five years.{e}

In his life on earth he surpassed all human beings except Enoch, because of his righteousness, in which he was perfect. Enoch’s office was ordained as a testimony for the generations of the world, to recount all the deeds of each generation until the day of judgment.

In the thirty-third jubilee, in the first year of the second week, Peleg took a wife named Lomna, daughter of Sinar, and in the fourth year of this week she bore him a son and he named him Reu; for he said, “Look, human beings have become evil, with the wicked plan of building themselves a city and a tower in the land of Shinar.”{f}
They left the land of Ararat and went east to Shinar, for in his days they built the city and the tower, saying, “Come, let us climb up by it into heaven.”

They began to build, and in the fourth week they made bricks with fire, and the bricks served them as stone, and the mortar they used to join them was asphalt, which comes out of the sea and from springs of water in the land of Shinar.

They built it for forty-three years. Its width was 203 bricks, and a brick was a third of a unit in height; its height came to 5,433 cubits and 2 palms, and one wall was thirteen stades long and the other thirty.{g}

The Lord our God said to us, “Look, they are one people, and this is what they have begun to do, and now nothing will be held back from them. Come, let us go down and confuse their language, so that they will not understand one another’s speech, and they will be scattered into cities and nations, and a single purpose will never again be among them until the day of judgment.”
The Lord came down, and we came down with him to see the city and the tower that human beings had built.
He confused their language, and they no longer understood one another’s speech, and then they stopped building the city and the tower.

For this reason the whole land of Shinar is called Babel, because the Lord confused all the language of humankind there, and from there they were scattered to their cities, each according to his language and his nation.
The Lord sent a mighty wind against the tower and threw it down to the earth. It lay between Asshur and Babylon in the land of Shinar, and they called it “Overthrow.”{h}
In the first year of the fourth week, at the beginning of the thirty-fourth jubilee, they were scattered from the land of Shinar.
Ham and his sons went into the land that he was to occupy, which he had acquired as his portion in the land of the south.{i}

Canaan saw that the land of Lebanon as far as the river of Egypt was very good, and he did not go to the land of his inheritance in the west, by the sea, but settled in the land of Lebanon, east and west, from the border of the Jordan and from the border of the sea.

His father Ham and his brothers Cush and Mizraim said to him, “You have settled in a land that is not yours, and did not fall to us by lot. Do not do it; for if you do, you and your sons will fall in the land and be cursed through rebellion; for you have settled by rebellion, and by rebellion your children will fall, and you will be rooted out forever.
Do not live in the dwelling of Shem, for it came to Shem and his sons by their lot.
You are cursed, and you will be cursed beyond all Noah’s sons, by the curse by which we bound ourselves with an oath before the holy judge and before Noah our father.”
But he did not listen to them, and settled in the land of Lebanon from Hamath to the entrance of Egypt, he and his sons, to this day.
For this reason that land is called Canaan.{j}

Japheth and his sons went toward the sea and settled in the land of their portion. Madai saw the land by the sea and did not like it, and begged a portion from Elam, Asshur, and Arpachshad, his wife’s brother, and settled in the land of Media, near his wife’s brother, to this day.
He named his dwelling and the dwelling of his sons Media, after the name of their father Madai.
