notes.text: Verses 1–15 are the other main piece of the “Book of Noah” (see ch. 7). The Hebrew original of verses 1–2 and 9–14 survives among the Dead Sea Scrolls, Charles noted. The “demons” are the spirits of the dead giants, the offspring of the Watchers and women (1 Enoch 15:8–12).

Mastema means “hostility” or “animosity” (Hebrew mastemah; compare Hos 9:7–8). Here he is the chief of the evil spirits, and in 11:5 and 17:16 he is identified with Satan, the Adversary. In the Dead Sea Scrolls he is called Belial.
Compare 1 Enoch 15–16, where all the demons are left free until the judgment.
The angel was Raphael, whose name means “God heals” (Tobit 3:17; 12:14–15).
Reu: sounds like Hebrew ra‘, “evil.”

The measurements of Jubilees, converted. A cubit is about 18 inches (45 cm), and a palm 3 inches (7.6 cm), so the 5,433 cubits and 2 palms is about 8,150 feet (2,484 m), a little more than a mile and a half. A stade is about 607 feet (185 m): thirteen stades is about 7,900 feet (2.4 km) and thirty stades about 18,200 feet (5.5 km). The numbers are legendary, and the text seems also confused.

The tower’s name in Jubilees is “Overthrow”; the real name was Babel (Hebrew bavel, a pun on balal, “confuse,” in Gen 11:9). Jewish tradition says that seventy nations were created at Babel, each under an angel.
“South” should read “north,” as Charles saw: Ham’s true portion was northwest Africa (8:22–24).
Canaan: the ancient pun is lost, but the book plays on the name as “a land seized by Canaan.”

chapters.heading: Demons, the Death of Noah, and the Tower of Babel

verses.text: In the thirty-fifth jubilee, in the first year of the third week, Reu took a wife named Ora, daughter of Ur, son of Kesed, and in the seventh year of this week, in this jubilee, she bore him a son and he named him Serug.

The sons of Noah began to fight one another, to take captives and kill one another, to shed human blood on the earth and eat blood, to build strong cities, walls, and towers; individuals began to raise themselves above the nation, to found the first kingdoms, and to go to war, people against people, nation against nation, and city against city. Everyone began to do evil, to acquire weapons, to teach their sons war, to capture cities, and to sell male and female slaves.{a}
Ur, son of Kesed, built the city of Ara of the Chaldeans, and named it after himself and his father.{b}

They made molten images for themselves, and each worshiped the idol, the molten image he had made. They began to make carved images and unclean likenesses, and malicious spirits helped and led them astray into transgression and uncleanness.

Prince Mastema worked hard to do all this, and sent out other spirits, those placed under his hand, to commit every sort of wrong and sin and transgression, to corrupt and destroy, and to shed blood on the earth.
For this reason he named Seroh “Serug,” because everyone turned to commit every sort of sin and transgression.{c}

He grew up and lived in Ur of the Chaldeans, near his wife’s mother’s father, and worshiped idols. He took a wife in the thirty-sixth jubilee, in the first year of the fifth week, named Melka, daughter of Kabor, his father’s brother’s daughter.

In the first year of that week she bore him Nahor, and he grew up and lived in Ur of the Chaldeans, and his father taught him the studies of the Chaldeans, to practice divination and augury by the signs of heaven.
In the thirty-seventh jubilee, in the first year of the sixth week, he took a wife named Iyaska, daughter of Nestag of the Chaldeans.
In the seventh year of this week she bore him Terah.

Prince Mastema sent ravens and birds to devour the seed that was sown in the land, to destroy the land and rob human beings of their labor. Before they could plow in the seed, the ravens picked it from the surface of the ground.
For this reason he named him Terah, because the ravens and the birds brought them to poverty and devoured their seed.{d}
The years began to be barren because of the birds, and they ate all the fruit from the trees; only with great effort could they save a little of all the fruit of the earth in their days.
In this thirty-ninth jubilee, in the first year of the second week, Terah took a wife named Edna, daughter of Abram, his father’s sister.
In the seventh year of this week she bore him a son, and he named him Abram, after the name of his mother’s father, for he had died before his daughter conceived.

The child began to understand the errors of the earth, that everyone had gone astray after carved images and uncleanness. His father taught him writing, and when he was two weeks of years old he separated himself from his father, so that he would not worship idols with him.{e}
He began to pray to the Creator of all things to save him from the errors of human beings, and that his portion would not fall into error after uncleanness and vileness.
The seedtime came for sowing seed on the land, and they all went out together to protect their seed from the ravens. Abram went with them, and the boy was fourteen years old.

A cloud of ravens came to eat the seed, and Abram ran to meet them before they landed on the ground, and cried to them before they landed to eat the seed, and said, “Do not come down; go back to where you came from,” and they began to turn back.
That day he made the clouds of ravens turn back seventy times, and not one raven stayed anywhere in the land where Abram was.
Everyone in the country who was with him saw him shout and watched every raven turn away; his name grew great throughout Chaldea.
That year all who wanted to sow came to him, and he went with them until the time of sowing ended. They sowed their land, and that year they brought home enough grain, and ate and were satisfied.

In the first year of the fifth week, Abram taught the makers of tools for oxen, the woodworkers, and they made a container above the ground, facing the frame of the plow, to hold the seed, so that the seed fell down from it onto the plowshare and was hidden in the earth, and they no longer feared the ravens.{f}
They made containers above the ground in the same way on all the plow frames, and they sowed and tilled all the land as Abram commanded them, and they no longer feared the birds.

notes.text: A note against monarchy: in this account the first kingdoms come from violence.
“Ur of the Chaldeans” (Gen 11:28) is here read as two persons’ names, Ur and Kesed.
Serug is linked to Hebrew sarar, “turn aside, rebel.”
The Hebrew pun on Terah is uncertain.

Two weeks of years: fourteen years old; Abram’s age is given as in the fourteen-year-old of verse 18. The story of Abram’s break with idolatry is the root of much later Jewish legend (compare the Apocalypse of Abraham).
A seed drill: an improvement on scattering by hand. Rabbinic tradition ascribes the plow to Noah.

chapters.heading: The Birth of Idolatry and the Family of Abram

verses.text: In the seventh year of the sixth week, Abram said to his father Terah, “Father!” He said, “Here I am, my son.”
He said, “What help and profit do we get from these idols you worship, and bow down to?
There is no spirit in them. They are dumb forms, and a deception of the heart. Do not worship them.
Worship the God of heaven, who sends the rain and the dew on the earth, and does everything on the earth, and made everything by his word; all life is from before his face.{a}

Why do you worship things that have no spirit in them? They are the work of human hands, and you carry them on your shoulders, and you have no help from them; they are a great shame to those who make them, and a deception of the heart to those who worship them. Do not worship them.”
His father said, “I know it too, my son, but what can I do with a people who have made me serve before them?
If I tell them the truth, they will kill me, for they are attached to them, to worship and honor them. Keep quiet, my son, or they will kill you.”
He said these things to his two brothers, and they were angry with him, and he kept quiet.
In the seventh year of the second week of the fortieth jubilee, Abram took a wife named Sarai, the daughter of his father, and she became his wife.{b}
Haran, his brother, took a wife in the third year of the third week, and in the seventh year of this week she bore him a son, and he named him Lot.
Nahor, his brother, took a wife.
In the sixtieth year of Abram’s life, in the fourth year of the fourth week, Abram got up by night and burned the house of the idols, and everything in it, and no one knew.{c}
They got up in the night and tried to save their gods from the middle of the fire.
Haran hurried to save them, but the fire flared over him, and he was burned in the fire and died in Ur of the Chaldeans before his father Terah, and they buried him in Ur of the Chaldeans.

Terah left Ur of the Chaldeans, he and his sons, to go to the land of Lebanon and the land of Canaan, and he settled in the land of Haran, and Abram lived with his father Terah in Haran for two weeks of years.{d}

In the fifth year of the sixth week, Abram sat up all night on the first day of the seventh month to watch the stars from evening to morning, to see what the year would be like for rain, and he sat alone watching.{e}
A thought rose in his heart, and he said, “The signs of the stars, and the paths of the sun and moon, all rest in the Lord’s hand. Why am I trying to investigate them?
If he wants, he sends rain, morning and evening; if he wants, he holds it back. Everything is in his hand.”
He prayed that night and said, “My God, God Most High, you alone are my God. I have chosen you and your dominion. You made everything, and everything that exists is the work of your hands.

Rescue me from the hands of the evil spirits who have power over the thoughts of human hearts, and do not let them lead me astray from you, my God. Establish me and my descendants forever, so that we do not go astray from now on and forever.”

He said, “Should I go back to Ur of the Chaldeans, where they are seeking my face to have me return to them, or am I to stay here in this place? Make the right path before you prosper in the hands of your servant, so that he may do it and not walk in the deceitfulness of my heart, my God.”

He finished speaking and praying, and the word of the Lord was sent to him through me, saying, “Leave your country, your relatives, and your father’s house for a land I will show you, and I will make you a great and numerous nation.

I will bless you and make your name great, and you will be blessed on the earth, and in you all the families of the earth will be blessed. I will bless those who bless you, and curse those who curse you.
I will be a God to you and to your son, and to your son’s son, and to all your descendants. Do not be afraid; from now on and for all generations of the earth I am your God.”

The Lord God said, “Open his mouth and his ears, so that he can hear and speak with his mouth in the language that has been revealed,” for it had stopped coming from the mouths of all human beings from the day of the overthrow of Babel.{f}
I opened his mouth, his ears, and his lips, and began to speak with him in Hebrew, the language of creation.

He took the books of his fathers, which were written in Hebrew, and copied them, and from then on began to study them, and I explained to him what he could not understand, and he studied them through the six rainy months.{g}
In the seventh year of the sixth week he spoke to his father and told him he was going to leave Haran to go to the land of Canaan, to see it and return to him.

His father Terah said to him, “Go in peace. May the eternal God make your path straight, and may the Lord be with you and protect you from all evil, and give you grace, mercy, and favor before those who see you, and may no human being have power over you to harm you. Go in peace.
If you see a land pleasant to your eyes to live in, then get up and take me to you, and take Lot with you, the son of Haran your brother, as your own son. The Lord be with you.
Leave your brother Nahor with me until you return in peace, and we will all go with you together.”

notes.text: Abram’s argument against idols closely follows Ps 115:4–8 and Jer 10:1–16. Its likeness to the Apocalypse of Abraham (chs. 1–8) shows both draw on one older legend.
Sarai is Abram’s half-sister (Gen 20:12). Later rabbis allowed such a marriage to Noah’s descendants, but it is forbidden in Lev 18:9; 20:17.
The sixtieth year of his life is the year of the world 1936 (nineteen centuries and thirty-six years after creation). Abram was born in 1876 (11:15).
Fourteen years.
The first day of the seventh month: about September 20 in the 364-day calendar, the beginning of the autumn rain season.
The “language that has been revealed” is Hebrew, said here to be the original tongue of all humankind, lost at Babel and restored to Abram. See 12:26–27 and 3:28.
The six rainy months: the winter half-year. Another tradition says that Eber alone kept Hebrew, because he took no part in building the tower.

chapters.heading: Abram Burns the Idols and Leaves Ur

verses.text: Abram left Haran, taking his wife Sarai and Lot, his brother Haran’s son, to the land of Canaan; he came to Asshur and went on to Shechem and settled near a tall oak.{a}
He saw that the land was very pleasant, from the entrance of Hamath to the tall oak.
The Lord said to him, “To you and your descendants I will give this land.”
He built an altar there and offered a burnt offering on it to the Lord, who had appeared to him.
He moved from there to the mountain between Bethel on the west and Ai on the east, and pitched his tent there.

He saw that the land was very wide and good, and everything grew on it: vines, figs, pomegranates, oaks, holm oaks, terebinths, olive trees, cedars, cypresses, date palms, and all the trees of the field, and there was water on the mountains.
He blessed the Lord, who had led him out of Ur of the Chaldeans and brought him to this land.
In the first year of the seventh week, on the first day of the first month, he built an altar on this mountain and called on the name of the Lord: “You, the eternal God, are my God.”{b}
He offered a burnt offering on the altar to the Lord, asking that he be with him and not leave him all the days of his life.

He moved from there and went south, and came to Hebron (Hebron was built at that time), and lived there for two years, and went from there into the southern land, to Bealoth, and there was a famine in the land.{c}
Abram went to Egypt in the third year of the week, and lived in Egypt for five years before his wife was taken from him.
Now Tanis in Egypt was built at that time, seven years after Hebron.{d}
When Pharaoh took Sarai, Abram’s wife, the Lord struck Pharaoh and his house with great plagues because of Sarai, Abram’s wife.
Abram became very rich in flocks, cattle, donkeys, horses, camels, male and female slaves, and in silver and gold in great quantity. Lot, his brother’s son, was also wealthy.

Pharaoh returned Sarai, Abram’s wife, and sent Abram away from Egypt. He went back to the spot where he had first set up his tent, the site of the altar, with Ai to the east and Bethel to the west, and he blessed the Lord his God for bringing him back safe.

In the third year of the first week of the forty-first jubilee he returned to this place and offered a burnt offering on it, and called on the name of the Lord, and said, “You, the Most High God, are my God forever and ever.”
In the fourth year of this week Lot parted from him, and Lot settled in Sodom, and the men of Sodom were very great sinners.
It grieved him in his heart that his brother’s son had left him, for he had no children.

In that year when Lot was taken captive, in the fourth year of this week, the Lord said to Abram after Lot had separated from him, “Lift up your eyes from the place where you are staying, north and south, west and east.

All the land you see I will give to you and your descendants forever, and I will make your descendants as the sand of the sea. Though a man could count the dust of the earth, your descendants will not be counted.
Get up, walk through the land, its length and its breadth, and see it all, for I will give it to your descendants.” Abram went to Hebron and lived there.

In this year Chedorlaomer, king of Elam, came with Amraphel, king of Shinar, Arioch, king of Sellasar, and Tergal, king of nations, and they killed the king of Gomorrah; the king of Sodom fled, and many fell wounded in the valley of Siddim by the Salt Sea.{e}
They took Sodom, Adam, and Zeboim captive, and they took Lot, the son of Abram’s brother, captive, with all his possessions, and went to Dan.{f}
Someone who had escaped came and told Abram that his brother’s son had been captured, and Abram armed his household servants.

. . . for Abram and his descendants, a tenth of the first fruits to the Lord, and the Lord ordained it as an ordinance forever, that they should give it to the priests who served before him, and that they should possess it forever.{g}
There is no limit of days to this law, for he ordained it for generations forever, that they should give the Lord the tenth of everything: of the seed, the wine, the oil, the cattle, and the sheep.
He gave it to his priests to eat and drink with joy before him.
The king of Sodom came to him and bowed before him, and said, “Our lord Abram, give us the people you have rescued, but keep the plunder.”

Abram said to him, “I lift up my hands to the Most High God: from a thread to a sandal strap I will not take anything of yours, so that you cannot say I made Abram rich; except only what the young men have eaten, and the share of the men who went with me, Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre. They will take their share.”

notes.text: Asshur: the Ethiopic is corrupt here; Charles read “Canaan.” The tall oak is that of Gen 12:6 (Moreh), as read by the Greek version.
The first day of the first month (about March 22, the new year) of the year 1954 from creation. Abram was seventy-five (Gen 12:4).
Bealoth: a town in the south of Judah (Josh 15:24).
Compare Num 13:22. Tanis is Zoan.
Sellasar is Ellasar. Tergal reads as in the Greek form of Tidal (Gen 14:1). The valley of Siddim is the Dead Sea area.
Adam is Admah.

The text has a gap before this verse. The missing lines must have told how Abram pursued the kings and met Melchizedek (Gen 14:15–20). Some Jews were uneasy that Abraham paid tithes to an uncircumcised priest, and one solution was to identify Melchizedek with Shem.

chapters.heading: Abram in Canaan and Egypt

verses.text: After these things, in the fourth year of this week, on the first day of the third month, the word of the Lord came to Abram in a dream: “Do not be afraid, Abram. I am your protector, and your reward will be very great.”{a}

He said, “Lord, Lord, what will you give me, since I am going away childless, and the son of Maseq, the son of my female slave, is Eliezer of Damascus; he will be my heir, and to me you have given no offspring.”
He said to him, “This man will not be your heir, but one who will come from your own body; he will be your heir.”
He brought him outside and said to him, “Look toward heaven and count the stars, if you are able to count them.”
He looked toward heaven and saw the stars. He said to him, “So will your descendants be.”
He believed in the Lord, and it was counted to him as righteousness.
He said to him, “I am the Lord who brought you out of Ur of the Chaldeans, to give you the land of the Canaanites to possess forever, and I will be God to you and to your descendants after you.”
He said, “Lord, Lord, how will I know that I will inherit it?”
He said to him, “Take me a heifer three years old, a goat three years old, a sheep three years old, a turtledove, and a pigeon.”
He took all these in the middle of the month, and lived by the oak of Mamre, near Hebron.
He built an altar there and sacrificed all of these, and poured their blood on the altar, and cut them in half and laid the pieces opposite each other; but he did not cut the birds.
Birds came down on the pieces, and Abram drove them away and did not let the birds touch them.

When the sun had set, a trance fell on Abram, and a horror of great darkness fell on him, and he was told, “Know for certain that your descendants will be foreigners in a land that is not theirs, and they will be made slaves and afflicted for four hundred years.{b}
I will judge the nation they serve, and after that they will come out with great wealth.
You will go to your fathers in peace, and be buried at a good old age.
But in the fourth generation they will return here, for the wrongdoing of the Amorites is not yet complete.”{c}
He woke from his sleep and got up, and the sun had set, and there was a flame, and a smoking furnace, and a flame of fire passed between the pieces.

On that day the Lord made a covenant with Abram, saying, “To your descendants I will give this land, from the river of Egypt to the great river, the river Euphrates: the Kenites, Kenizzites, Kadmonites, Perizzites, Rephaim, Phakorites, Hivites, Amorites, Canaanites, Girgashites, and Jebusites.”
The day passed, and Abram offered the pieces and the birds, with their grain offerings and drink offerings, and the fire consumed them.
On that day we made a covenant with Abram, as we had made a covenant with Noah in this month, and Abram renewed the festival and ordinance for himself forever.{d}
Abram rejoiced and told all these things to his wife Sarai, and he believed he would have offspring, but she did not bear.
Sarai advised her husband Abram and said to him, “Go in to my Egyptian slave Hagar; perhaps I will build up descendants for you through her.”
Abram listened to the voice of his wife Sarai and said to her, “Do so.” Sarai took her Egyptian slave Hagar and gave her to her husband Abram to be his wife.
He went in to her, and she conceived and bore him a son, and he named him Ishmael, in the fifth year of this week; this was the eighty-sixth year of Abram’s life.{e}

notes.text: First day of the third month: about May 22. The covenant itself is made on the fifteenth day of the same month (verses 10 and 20), the day of the Feast of Weeks (about June 5).
Four hundred years: Gen 15:13. Exod 12:40 has 430, and Paul counts 430 from the promise (Gal 3:17). In Jubilees the four hundred years run from the birth of Isaac.
A generation here is a hundred years.
On that day: the fifteenth of the third month (see 6:17–22), the Feast of Weeks.
The year 1965 from creation.

chapters.heading: God’s Covenant with Abram, and the Birth of Ishmael

verses.text: In the fifth year of the fourth week of this jubilee, in the third month, in the middle of the month, Abram celebrated the feast of the first fruits of the grain harvest.{a}

He offered new offerings on the altar, the first fruits of the produce, to the Lord: a heifer, a goat, and a sheep on the altar as a burnt offering to the Lord; he offered their grain offerings and drink offerings on the altar with frankincense.
The Lord appeared to Abram and said to him, “I am God Almighty; show yourself faithful before me and be perfect.
I will make my covenant between me and you, and I will multiply you greatly.”
Abram fell on his face, and God talked with him and said,
“See, my ordinance is with you, and you will be the father of many nations.
You will no longer be called Abram, but from now on your name, forever, will be Abraham, for I have made you the father of many nations.{b}
I will make you very great, and make you into nations, and kings will come out of you.
I will establish my covenant between me and you, and your descendants after you, through their generations, as an eternal covenant, so that I may be God to you and to your descendants after you.
I will give you and your descendants after you the land where you have been a stranger, the land of Canaan, to possess forever, and I will be their God.”

The Lord said to Abraham, “As for you, keep my covenant, you and your descendants after you. Circumcise every male among you, circumcise your foreskins, and it will be the sign of an eternal covenant between me and you.

You will circumcise the child on the eighth day, every male through your generations, whether born in the house or bought with money from any foreigner, anyone you have acquired who is not of your descendants.{c}
The one born in your house will certainly be circumcised, and those you buy with money will be circumcised, and my covenant will be in your flesh as an eternal ordinance.
The uncircumcised male who is not circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin on the eighth day will be cut off from his people, for he has broken my covenant.”
God said to Abraham, “As for your wife Sarai, her name will no longer be called Sarai; Sarah will be her name.{d}
I will bless her, and give you a son by her, and I will bless him, and he will become a nation, and kings of nations will come from him.”
Abraham fell on his face and rejoiced, and said in his heart, “Will a son be born to a man a hundred years old, and will Sarah, who is ninety, bear a child?”
Abraham said to God, “If only Ishmael might live before you!”
God said, “Yes, and Sarah also will bear you a son, and you will name him Isaac, and I will establish my covenant with him, an everlasting covenant, and with his descendants after him.{e}
As for Ishmael also, I have heard you, and I will bless him and make him great and multiply him greatly, and he will father twelve princes, and I will make him a great nation.
But I will establish my covenant with Isaac, whom Sarah will bear you, in these days, in the next year.”
He stopped speaking with him, and God went up from Abraham.
Abraham did what God had told him. He took his son Ishmael, all who had been born in his household, and all he had purchased, every male of his house, and circumcised the flesh of their foreskins.
On that very day Abraham was circumcised, and all the men of his house, those born in the house and all those he had bought with money from foreigners were circumcised with him.

This law is for all generations forever, and there is no postponing the circumcision, and no skipping one day out of the eight; for it is an eternal ordinance, ordained and written on the heavenly tablets.

Every male who is born and whose foreskin is not circumcised on the eighth day does not belong to the children of the covenant that the Lord made with Abraham, but to the children of destruction; nor is there any mark on him that he is the Lord’s; he is destined to be destroyed and killed from the earth, and rooted out of the earth, for he has broken the covenant of the Lord our God.

All the angels of the presence and all the angels of holiness have been made like this since the day they were created, and in front of them he consecrated Israel, so that Israel would be with him and with his holy angels.{f}
Tell the Israelites to keep the sign of this covenant in every generation as a perpetual law, and they will never be uprooted from the land.
For the command is ordained as a covenant, to be kept forever among all the Israelites.

The Lord did not bring Ishmael, his sons, his brothers, and Esau near to himself, and he did not choose them, though they are Abraham’s children, because he knew them; but he chose Israel to be his people.

He made them holy and gathered them from all of humankind; for there are many nations and many peoples, and all are his, and over all he has placed spirits in authority to lead them astray from him.{g}

Over Israel, though, he set no angel and no spirit as ruler, because he alone governs them. He himself will guard them and call them to account at the hands of his angels, his spirits, and all his hosts, so that he keeps them and blesses them, and so that they belong to him and he to them, now and always.

I now tell you that the Israelites will prove unfaithful to this law. They will not circumcise their sons in keeping with all this law; they will leave out circumcision of the flesh for their sons, and all of them, sons of Beliar, will leave their sons uncircumcised, just as they were born.{h}

There will be great wrath from the Lord against the Israelites, because they have abandoned his covenant, turned aside from his word, provoked and blasphemed, since they do not keep the ordinance of this law; for they have treated their members like the nations, so that they will be removed and rooted out of the land. There will be no more pardon or forgiveness for them, for all the sin of this eternal error.

notes.text: The “fourth” week should read “third” (Charles). The middle of the third month is the fifteenth, the Feast of Weeks (about June 5). The Pharisees counted the feast differently, on the sixth of Sivan.
Abraham: understood as “father of a multitude.”
Jubilees insists on the eighth day, as in the Greek and Samaritan texts of Gen 17:14.
Sarah: “princess.”
Isaac: “he laughs.”
The two highest ranks of angels share with Israel the keeping of the sabbath (2:18–21) and, here, circumcision; they were “created circumcised.”

Compare Deut 32:8–9 in the Greek version, where the nations are assigned to “angels of God.” Seventy nations were put under seventy angels, but Israel under none (verse 32); compare Dan 10:13, 20–21, where Michael is Israel’s prince.

Beliar: another form of Belial, “worthless”; here a name of the chief evil spirit. The author seems to be writing in a time when many Jews abandoned circumcision (the age of Antiochus Epiphanes, c. 170 BC).

chapters.heading: The Feast of First Fruits, Circumcision, and the Promise of Isaac

verses.text: On the first day of the fourth month we appeared to Abraham at the oak of Mamre and talked with him, and told him that a son would be given him by his wife Sarah.{a}
Sarah laughed, for she heard that we had said these words to Abraham, and we warned her, and she became afraid and denied that she had laughed at the words.
We named her son for her, as his name stands decreed and written on the heavenly tablets: Isaac.
We also said that when we came back to her at the appointed time, she would be carrying a son.

In this month the Lord carried out his judgments on Sodom, Gomorrah, Zeboim, and the whole region of the Jordan, and burned them with fire and sulfur and destroyed them to this day, as I have told you all their deeds: that they are exceedingly wicked and sinful, and defile themselves and commit fornication in their flesh, and work uncleanness on the earth.
In the same way God will execute judgment on the places where they do the same uncleanness as the Sodomites, like the judgment of Sodom.
But we saved Lot, for God remembered Abraham and sent him out from the middle of the overthrow.
He and his daughters committed a sin on the earth such as had not been on the earth from the days of Adam until his time; for the man lay with his daughters.

It was commanded and engraved on the heavenly tablets concerning all his descendants to remove them and root them out, and to execute judgment on them like the judgment of Sodom, and to leave no descendant of the man on earth on the day of condemnation.{b}
In this month Abraham moved from Hebron, and went and lived between Kadesh and Shur, in the mountains of Gerar.
In the middle of the fifth month he moved from there and lived at the Well of the Oath.{c}
In the middle of the sixth month the Lord visited Sarah and did to her as he had said, and she conceived.
She bore a son in the third month, in the middle of the month, at the time the Lord had told Abraham, on the festival of the first fruits of the harvest, and Isaac was born.{d}
Abraham circumcised his son on the eighth day. He was the first to be circumcised according to the covenant ordained forever.
In the sixth year of the fourth week we came to Abraham at the Well of the Oath, and appeared to him.

We blessed him and told him everything that had been decreed about him: that he would not die until he fathered six more sons and saw them before he died, but that his name and descendants would be called in Isaac.{e}
All the descendants of his other sons would be Gentiles and be counted with the Gentiles; but from the sons of Isaac one would become a holy line, and would not be counted among the Gentiles.

For he would become the portion of the Most High, and all his descendants would fall into God’s possession, to be a people for the Lord’s own possession above all nations, a kingdom, priests, and a holy nation.{f}
We went on our way and told Sarah all that we had told him, and they both rejoiced with very great joy.

He built an altar there to the Lord, who had rescued him and made him rejoice in the land where he stayed as a stranger, and he celebrated a festival of joy in this month for seven days, near the altar he had built at the Well of the Oath.{g}
He built booths for himself and his servants for this festival, and he was the first to celebrate the Feast of Tabernacles on earth.

During these seven days he brought a burnt offering to the altar each day for the Lord: two oxen, two rams, seven sheep, and one male goat as a sin offering, to make atonement for himself and his descendants.

And as a thank offering: seven rams, seven kids, seven sheep, and seven male goats, with their grain offerings and drink offerings; he burned all their fat on the altar, a chosen offering to the Lord for a pleasing fragrance.
Morning and evening he burned fragrant substances: frankincense, galbanum, stacte, nard, myrrh, spice, and costum. He offered all seven, ground and mixed together in equal parts, pure.
He kept this feast for seven days, rejoicing with all his heart and soul, he and all those in his house; there was no foreigner with him, and no one uncircumcised.

He blessed his Creator, who had made him in his generation, for he had made him according to his good pleasure; for he knew and saw that from him would rise the plant of righteousness for the eternal generations, and a holy line from him, so that it would become like him who made all things.{h}
He blessed and rejoiced, and called this festival the festival of the Lord, a joy acceptable to the Most High God.
We blessed him without end, and all the offspring who would come after him, in every generation of the earth, since he had kept this feast in its proper season, as the heavenly tablets testify.

For this reason it is ordained on the heavenly tablets concerning Israel that they celebrate the Feast of Tabernacles for seven days with joy, in the seventh month, acceptable before the Lord: a statute forever through their generations, every year.{i}
To this there is no limit of days; it is ordained forever for Israel that they celebrate it, live in booths, put wreaths on their heads, and take leafy branches and willows from the brook.

Abraham took palm branches and the fruit of fine trees, and every day he went around the altar with the branches seven times in the morning, and praised and thanked his God for everything with joy.{j}

notes.text: First day of the fourth month: about June 21. Compare Gen 18.
The descendants of Lot are Moab and Ammon (Gen 19:37–38).
The Well of the Oath is Beersheba (Gen 21:31). The middle of the fifth month is about August 5.
In the middle of the third month, the Feast of Weeks (about June 5), in the year 1987 from creation. Charles and others noted that the sixth month is actually meant, so the pregnancy is nine months.
Charles saw bracketed words here as a later insertion. The six sons are by Keturah (Gen 25:2).
Compare Exod 19:5–6. The Hebrew text has “a kingdom of priests”; Jubilees has a form closer to Rev 1:6; 5:10.
Verses 20–31 describe the origin of the Feast of Tabernacles, with several features of its own.
The plant of righteousness: compare 1 Enoch 10:16; 93:5, 10.
Seventh month: the fifteenth day is about October 4. Compare Lev 23:34–43.
In later Jewish practice, the seven circuits of the altar were made only on the seventh day.

chapters.heading: The Promise Renewed, Sodom Destroyed, and Isaac Born

verses.text: In the first year of the fifth week, in this jubilee, Isaac was weaned, and Abraham gave a great banquet in the third month, on the day his son Isaac was weaned.{a}
Ishmael, the son of Hagar the Egyptian, stood in front of his father Abraham in his place. Abraham was glad and blessed God, since he had lived to see his sons and had not died without children.

He remembered the words God had spoken to him on the day Lot left him, and he rejoiced because the Lord had given him descendants on the earth to inherit the earth, and he blessed the Creator of all things with his whole mouth.

Sarah watched Ishmael play and dance, and Abraham delighted in him. She grew jealous and said to Abraham, “Drive out this slave girl and her son. The slave girl’s son will never share the inheritance with my son Isaac.”{b}
This was hard for Abraham, because of his female slave and because of his son, that he should send them away from him.

God said to Abraham, “Do not let it be hard for you because of the boy and the slave woman. In everything Sarah has said to you, listen to her words and do them, for in Isaac your name and descendants will be called.
But as for the son of this slave woman, I will make him a great nation, because he is of your descendants.”
Abraham got up early in the morning and took bread and a skin of water, put them on the shoulders of Hagar and the boy, and sent her away.
She left and wandered in the desert of Beersheba, and the water in the skin ran out, and the boy was thirsty and could not go on, and he fell down.
His mother took him and threw him under an olive tree, and went and sat down opposite him, a bowshot away, for she said, “Let me not see my child die,” and as she sat she wept.
An angel of God, one of the holy ones, said to her, “Why are you weeping, Hagar? Get up, take the boy and hold him by the hand, for God has heard your voice and seen the boy.”
She opened her eyes, and saw a well of water, and went and filled her skin with water and gave her child a drink; she got up and went toward the desert of Paran.
The boy grew and became an archer, and God was with him. His mother took him a wife from the daughters of Egypt.
She bore him a son, and he named him Nebaioth, for she said, “The Lord was near me when I called on him.”{c}

In the seventh week, in its first year, in the first month of this jubilee, on the twelfth of the month, there were voices in heaven about Abraham, that he was faithful in all that God told him, that he loved the Lord, and that in every affliction he was faithful.{d}

Prince Mastema came and said before God, “See, Abraham loves his son Isaac and delights in him above all else; tell him to offer him as a burnt offering on the altar, and you will see whether he will do this, and you will know if he is faithful in everything you test him with.”{e}

The Lord knew that Abraham was faithful in all his afflictions, for he had tested him by his country, and with famine, and with the wealth of kings, and again through his wife, when she was taken from him, and with circumcision, and through Ishmael and Hagar his slave when he sent them away.{f}
In every trial he was found trustworthy. He did not grow impatient or hesitate to act, because he was loyal and loved the Lord.

notes.text: Isaac was weaned about the year 1989 from creation. The text says “fifth”; Charles read “fourth.”
Playing and dancing: the Greek and Latin of Gen 21:9 have “playing with her son Isaac.” The word “dancing” in Jubilees may be a copyist’s change.
Nebaioth was Ishmael’s eldest son (Gen 25:13). The explanation of the name here is not found in Genesis.
The twelfth of the first month is about April 2, in the year 2003 from creation. By the book’s own count, Isaac is twenty-three at the time (the Seder Olam rabbah says thirty-seven).
In Genesis God himself tests Abraham (Gen 22:1); here it is Mastema’s suggestion, as in Job 1–2.
Seven of Abraham’s ten traditional trials are named here. The others are Sarah’s barrenness, the offering of Isaac, and the burial of Sarah; other lists differ slightly.

chapters.heading: Hagar and Ishmael Sent Away, and Mastema’s Challenge

verses.text: God said to him, “Abraham, Abraham!” He said, “Here I am.”
He said, “Take your beloved son, whom you love, Isaac, and go to the high country and offer him on one of the mountains that I will point out to you.”

He got up early in the morning and saddled his donkey, and took two young men with him, and his son Isaac, and split the wood for the burnt offering, and went to the place on the third day, and saw the place from far away.
He came to a well of water, and said to his young men, “Stay here with the donkey, and I and the boy will go over there, and when we have worshiped we will come back to you.”
He took the wood of the burnt offering and laid it on his son Isaac, and took in his hand the fire and the knife, and the two of them went together to that place.
Isaac said to his father, “Father,” and he said, “Here I am, my son.” He said to him, “Here are the fire, the knife, and the wood; but where is the sheep for the burnt offering, father?”
He said, “God will provide a sheep for himself for a burnt offering, my son.” He came near to the place on the mount of God.
He built an altar and set the wood on it, and tied up his son Isaac and laid him on the wood on the altar, and stretched out his hand to take the knife to kill his son Isaac.
I stood before him, and before the prince Mastema, and the Lord said, “Tell him not to lay his hand on the boy or do anything to him, for I have shown that he fears the Lord.”{a}
I called to him from heaven and said to him, “Abraham, Abraham!” and he was terrified and said, “Here I am.”
I said to him, “Do not lay your hand on the boy and do not do anything to him, for now I have shown that you fear the Lord, and have not held back your son, your firstborn son, from me.”

Prince Mastema was put to shame, and Abraham lifted his eyes and looked, and there was a single ram caught . . . by its horns, and Abraham went and took the ram and offered it as a burnt offering in place of his son.{b}
Abraham called that place “The Lord has seen,” so that it is said, “On the mountain the Lord has seen”; that is Mount Zion.{c}
The Lord called Abraham by his name a second time from heaven, as he made us appear to speak to him in the name of the Lord.

He said, “I have sworn by myself, says the Lord: Because you have done this, and have not held back your son, your beloved son, from me, I will bless you and multiply your descendants like the stars of heaven and like the sand on the seashore. Your descendants will inherit the cities of their enemies,
and in your descendants all the nations of the earth will be blessed, because you have obeyed my voice, and I have shown everyone that you are faithful to me in all I have said to you. Go in peace.”
Abraham went to his young men, and they got up and went together to Beersheba, and Abraham lived by the Well of the Oath.
He celebrated this festival every year, seven days with joy, and called it the festival of the Lord, after the seven days during which he went and returned in peace.{d}
So it has been ordained and written on the heavenly tablets concerning Israel and its descendants that they keep this festival seven days with festival joy.

notes.text: The speaker is the angel of the presence, who is narrating to Moses. “Mastema” here is probably a class name for evil spirits, and not only their prince. Compare 10:8.
The text has a gap; Gen 22:13 adds “in a thicket.”
Mount Zion is identified with the mountain of Moriah, as in 2 Chron 3:1.

The seven days: the Feast of Passover and Unleavened Bread (the fifteenth to the twenty-first of the first month, about April 5–11). Jubilees places Isaac’s offering on the twelfth of the first month (17:15) and connects the seven days to the Passover season.

chapters.heading: The Offering of Isaac

verses.text: In the first year of the first week of the forty-second jubilee, Abraham returned and lived opposite Hebron, that is, Kiriath Arba, for two weeks of years.
In the first year of the second week of this jubilee, the days of Sarah’s life were completed, and she died in Hebron.{a}
Abraham went to grieve for her and bury her, and we put him to the test, to see whether his spirit was steady and whether he would hold his tongue. He proved steady in this and was not shaken.
For in patience of spirit he spoke with the Hittites, so that they would give him a place to bury his dead.
The Lord gave him favor before all who saw him, and he asked the Hittites gently, and they gave him the land of the double cave opposite Mamre, that is, Hebron, for four hundred pieces of silver.{b}

They begged him, saying, “We will give it to you for nothing,” but he would not take it from their hands for nothing, for he paid the price of the place, the money in full, and he bowed to them twice; after this he buried his dead in the double cave.
All the days of Sarah’s life were a hundred and twenty-seven years, that is, two jubilees, four weeks, and one year. These are the days of Sarah’s life.
This is the tenth trial with which Abraham was tested, and he was found faithful and patient in spirit.{c}

He said nothing at all about the rumor in the land that God had promised it to him and his descendants. He begged for a burial place there for his dead. He was found faithful and was written on the heavenly tablets as God’s friend.{d}

In the fourth year of this week he took a wife for his son Isaac, named Rebecca, the sister of Laban and daughter of Bethuel; Bethuel was the son of Melca, who was the wife of Nahor, Abraham’s brother.
Abraham took a third wife, named Keturah, from among the daughters of his household servants, for Hagar had died before Sarah.{e}
She bore him six sons: Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah, in the two weeks of years.
In the second year of the sixth week, Rebecca bore Isaac two sons, Jacob and Esau. Jacob was a smooth and upright man, and Esau was fierce, a man of the field, and hairy, and Jacob lived in tents.
The boys grew up. Jacob learned to write; Esau did not, for he was an outdoorsman and a hunter. He learned warfare, and everything he did was savage.{f}
Abraham loved Jacob, but Isaac loved Esau.

Abraham saw Esau’s deeds, and knew that his name and descendants would be called in Jacob. He called Rebecca and gave her instructions about Jacob, for he knew that she also loved Jacob much more than Esau.
He said to her, “My daughter, watch over my son Jacob, for he will be in my place on the earth, a blessing among human beings and the glory of all the descendants of Shem.
For I know that the Lord will choose him to be a people for his own possession above all peoples on the face of the earth.
See, my son Isaac loves Esau more than Jacob, but I see that you truly love Jacob.
Add still more to your kindness to him, and let your eyes be on him in love, for he will be a blessing to us on the earth from now on through all generations of the earth.
May your hands be strong and your heart be glad in your son Jacob, whom I love far more than all my other sons. He will be blessed forever, and his offspring will fill the entire earth.
If a man can count the sand of the earth, his descendants also will be counted.
All the blessings with which the Lord has blessed me and my descendants will belong to Jacob and his descendants always.
In his descendants my name will be blessed, and the name of my fathers, Shem, Noah, Enoch, Mahalalel, Enos, Seth, and Adam.{g}
These will serve to lay the foundations of heaven, to strengthen the earth, and to renew all the lights in the sky.”
He called Jacob before the eyes of his mother Rebecca, and kissed him and blessed him, and said,

“Jacob, my beloved son, whom my soul loves, may God bless you from above the firmament, and give you all the blessings with which he blessed Adam, Enoch, Noah, and Shem; and all the things he told me and all he promised to give me, may he make them stay with you and your descendants forever, as long as the days of heaven above the earth.
May the spirits of Mastema not rule over you or your descendants to turn you from the Lord, who is your God from now on forever.
May the Lord God be a father to you, and you the firstborn son, and to the people always. Go in peace, my son.”
They both went out together from Abraham.
Rebecca loved Jacob with all her heart and all her soul, much more than Esau, but Isaac loved Esau much more than Jacob.

notes.text: The text says “third”; Charles read “second.”
The double cave is Machpelah (Gen 23).
Compare 17:17 and the note there.
“Friend of God”: compare Isa 41:8 and Jas 2:23.
This explains why Abraham did not take Hagar back. A later tradition identifies Hagar and Keturah.
In the Aramaic Targums, the “tents” are schools. Jacob is portrayed throughout as a lifelong student of the law.
Methuselah is left out of the list, and Adam is counted among the holy ancestors.

chapters.heading: Sarah’s Death, Rebecca, and Abraham’s Blessing of Jacob

verses.text: In the first year of the sixth week of the forty-second jubilee, Abraham called Ishmael and his twelve sons, Isaac and his two sons, and the six sons of Keturah and their sons.{a}

He commanded them to keep the way of the Lord, to practice righteousness, to love their neighbors, and to act this way among all people; each of them was to walk so as to do justice and righteousness on the earth.

They were to circumcise their sons, according to the covenant he had made with them, and not turn to the right or left from any of the paths the Lord had commanded us; and we were to keep ourselves from all fornication and uncleanness.{b}

If any woman or girl commits fornication among you, burn her with fire, and do not let them commit fornication with her in their eyes and hearts; and do not let them take wives from the daughters of Canaan, for the descendants of Canaan will be rooted out of the land.{c}
He spoke to them about the judgment on the giants and on the people of Sodom, how they were condemned for their wickedness and died for their sexual immorality, impurity, and corrupting one another.

“Guard yourselves from all fornication and uncleanness and every pollution of sin, or you will make our name a curse and your whole life a laughingstock, and all your sons will be destroyed by the sword, and you will become cursed like Sodom and all your remnant like the sons of Gomorrah.
I beg you, my sons: love the God of heaven and hold on to all his commandments. Do not walk after their idols and their uncleanness.

Do not make molten or carved gods for yourselves, for they are empty, and there is no spirit in them; they are the work of human hands, and all who trust in them trust in nothing. Do not serve them or worship them.

Serve the Most High God and worship him continually; hope always for his face, and practice uprightness and righteousness before him, so that he will take pleasure in you and give you his mercy, and send you rain morning and evening, and bless all the work you do on the earth, and bless your bread and your water, the fruit of your womb and the fruit of your land, the herds of your cattle and the flocks of your sheep.
You will be a blessing on the earth, and all the nations of the earth will desire you and bless their sons in my name, so that they may be blessed as I am.”
He gave gifts to Ishmael and his sons, and to the sons of Keturah, and sent them away from his son Isaac, and he gave everything to his son Isaac.
Ishmael and his sons, and the sons of Keturah and their sons, went together and settled from Paran to the entrance of Babylon, in all the land east of there facing the desert.
They mingled with each other, and their name was called Arabs and Ishmaelites.

notes.text: The text says “seventh”; Charles read “sixth.”
Circumcision is binding also on the descendants of Ishmael and Keturah; Esau’s line is left out.
The law of Moses prescribes burning only for a priest’s daughter (Lev 21:9); in other cases, stoning.

chapters.heading: Abraham’s Last Instructions

verses.text: In the sixth year of the seventh week of this jubilee, Abraham called his son Isaac and commanded him, saying, “I have become old and do not know the day of my death; I am full of my days.{a}
I am a hundred and seventy-five years old, and all the days of my life I have remembered the Lord, and have sought with all my heart to do his will and to walk uprightly in all his ways.
My soul has hated idols, and I have despised those who served them, and I have given my heart and spirit to observe the will of him who made me.

For he is the living God, holy and faithful, and he is righteous beyond all, and with him there is no favoritism and no accepting of gifts, for God is righteous and executes judgment on all who transgress his commandments and despise his covenant.
You, my son, keep his commandments, ordinances, and judgments, and do not walk after the abominations, the carved images, and the molten images.
Do not eat any blood of animals or livestock, or of any bird that flies in the sky.

When you slaughter an animal as an acceptable peace offering, do so and pour its blood over the altar. Burn all the offering’s fat on the altar together with fine flour, the grain offering mixed with oil, and its drink offering, all of it on the burnt-offering altar. It is a fragrance pleasing to the Lord.

You will offer the fat of the thank offering on the fire that is on the altar: the fat on the belly, all the fat on the inner parts, and the two kidneys and all the fat on them, and on the loins; and you will remove the liver along with the kidneys.
Offer all these as a pleasing fragrance, acceptable before the Lord, with its grain offering and drink offering, the bread of the offering to the Lord.

Eat the meat that day and the next, but before the sun sets on the second day it must be eaten. Leave nothing for the third day, because then it is unacceptable and may not be eaten anymore, and whoever eats it will load sin on himself. This is what I found written in my ancestors’ books, in Enoch’s words, and in Noah’s.{b}
On all offerings you will sprinkle salt, and do not let the salt of the covenant be missing from any of your offerings before the Lord.

As for the wood of the sacrifices, be careful not to bring any other wood to the altar except these: cypress, dafran, sagad, pine, fir, cedar, savin, palm, olive, myrtle, laurel, citron, juniper, and balsam.{c}

From these woods, put on the altar beneath the sacrifice only pieces that have been checked for appearance. Do not lay cracked or dark wood on it, but hard, clean, flawless, sound wood from fresh growth. Do not lay old wood there, since its scent is gone; it no longer smells as it once did.
Besides these woods there is no other that you may place on the altar, for the fragrance is dispersed, and the smell of its fragrance does not go up to heaven.
Keep this commandment and do it, my son, so that you may be upright in all your deeds.

At all times be clean in your body, and wash yourself with water before you approach to offer on the altar, and wash your hands and feet before you come near the altar; when you are done sacrificing, wash your hands and feet again.
Let no blood appear on you or on your clothes. Guard yourself, my son, against blood, be very careful; cover it with dust.
Do not eat any blood, for it is the soul; eat no blood at all.

Take no gifts for human blood, or it will be shed with impunity, without judgment; for it is shed blood that makes the earth sin, and the earth cannot be cleansed from human blood except by the blood of the one who shed it.

Take no present or gift for human blood: blood for blood, so that you may be accepted before the Lord, the Most High God; for he is the defense of the good; so that you may be kept from all evil, and he may save you from every kind of death.
I see, my son, that all the works of human beings are sin and wickedness, and all their deeds are uncleanness, an abomination, and a pollution, and there is no righteousness in them.

Take care not to walk in their ways and tread their paths, and not to commit a sin unto death before the Most High God, or he will hide his face from you and give you back into the hands of your transgression, and root you out of the land, and your descendants likewise from under heaven, and your name and your descendants will vanish from the whole earth.
Turn away from all their deeds and all their uncleanness, and keep the ordinance of the Most High God, and do his will and be upright in all things.

He will bless you in all your deeds, and will raise up from you the plant of righteousness through all the earth, throughout all generations of the earth, and my name and your name will not be forgotten under heaven forever.

Go, my son, in peace. May the Most High God, my God and yours, strengthen you to do his will, and may he bless all your descendants and the rest of your descendants through the generations forever, with all righteous blessings, so that you may be a blessing on all the earth.”
He went out from him rejoicing.

notes.text: The text says “seventh”; Charles read “sixth.” These words are Isaac’s in Gen 27:2. The rest of the chapter gives Abraham’s directions to Isaac on sacrifice, a parallel to Testament of Levi 9, where Isaac teaches Levi.
These rules about the sacrificial meat are not found in the surviving writings of Enoch or Noah.
Fourteen kinds of wood. The Mishnah allows any wood except olive and vine. Dafran and sagad are unknown trees; the Ethiopic words are transcribed.

chapters.heading: Abraham’s Last Words to Isaac

verses.text: In the first week of the forty-second jubilee, in the sixth year, the year Abraham died, Isaac and Ishmael came from the Well of the Oath to celebrate the Feast of Weeks, the harvest feast of first fruits, with their father Abraham. Abraham was glad that both his sons had come.{a}
Isaac had many possessions in Beersheba, and he used to go and see his possessions and return to his father.
At that time Ishmael came to visit his father. The two came together, and Isaac presented a burnt offering on his father’s altar, the one Abraham had built in Hebron.

He offered a thank offering and made a feast of joy before his brother Ishmael, and Rebecca made new cakes from the new grain and gave them to her son Jacob to take to his father Abraham, from the first fruits of the land, so that he could eat and bless the Creator of all things before he died.
Isaac also sent by Jacob’s hand to Abraham a fine thank offering, so that he could eat and drink.

He ate and drank, and blessed the Most High God, who made heaven and earth, who made all the rich things of the earth and gave them to human beings, so that they could eat and drink and bless their Creator.
“Now I give thanks to you, my God, because you have let me see this day. Look, I am a hundred and seventy-five years old, an old man and full of days, and all my days have been peace to me.
The sword of the enemy has not overcome me in anything you gave me and my children all the days of my life to this day.

My God, may your mercy and your peace be on your servant and on the descendants of his sons, so that they may be a chosen nation and an inheritance for you from among all the nations of the earth from now on through all the days of the generations of the earth, through all the ages.”

He called Jacob and said, “My son Jacob, may the God of all bless you and strengthen you to do righteousness and his will before him, and may he choose you and your descendants to be a people for his inheritance according to his will always. Come near, my son Jacob, and kiss me.”

He came near and kissed him, and Abraham said, “Blessed be my son Jacob and all the sons of God Most High, through all the ages. May God give you a righteous line, and may he make some of your sons holy in the middle of the whole earth. May nations serve you, and all the nations bow down to your descendants.{b}
Be strong in the presence of people, and rule over all the descendants of Seth. Then your ways and your sons’ ways will be justified, so that they become a holy nation.{c}

May the Most High God give you all the blessings with which he blessed me and with which he blessed Noah and Adam; may they rest on the holy head of your descendants from generation to generation forever.

May he cleanse you from all unrighteousness and impurity, so that you may be forgiven all your transgressions and your sins of ignorance. May he strengthen you and bless you, and may you inherit the whole earth.

May he renew his covenant with you, so that you may be a nation for his inheritance for all the ages, and so that he may be to you and your descendants a God in truth and righteousness through all the days of the earth.

You, my son Jacob, remember my words and keep the commandments of Abraham your father: separate yourself from the nations, do not eat with them, do not act as they do, and do not become their partner, for their works are unclean, and all their ways are a pollution, an abomination, and uncleanness.{d}
They offer sacrifices to the dead and worship evil spirits, and eat over the graves, and all their works are vanity and nothingness.
They lack the mind to understand, and their eyes cannot see their own deeds or how they go astray, telling a block of wood, ‘You are my God,’ and a stone, ‘You are my Lord, you save me.’
As for you, my son Jacob, may the Most High God help you, and the God of heaven bless you and remove you from their uncleanness and all their error.
Be careful, my son Jacob, not to take a wife from any of the daughters of Canaan, for all his descendants are to be rooted out of the earth.

For, because of the transgression of Ham, Canaan erred, and all his descendants will be destroyed from the earth with all the rest of them, and none who come from him will be saved on the day of judgment.

And all the worshipers of idols and the profane will have no hope in the land of the living; there will be no remembrance of them on the earth, for they will go down to Sheol and into the place of condemnation. As the children of Sodom were taken from the earth, so all who worship idols will be taken away.
Do not be afraid, my son Jacob, and do not be dismayed, son of Abraham. May the Most High God keep you from destruction, and deliver you from all the paths of error.

I built this house for myself, to put my name on it on the earth; it is given to you and your descendants forever, and it will be named the house of Abraham; it is given to you and your descendants forever; for you will build my house and establish my name before God forever; your descendants and your name will stand through all generations of the earth.”{e}
He stopped commanding him and blessing him.
The two of them lay down together in one bed. Jacob slept against the chest of his grandfather Abraham, who kissed him seven times, his heart and his love glad over the boy.

He blessed him with all his heart and said, “The Most High God, the God of all, Creator of all, who brought me out of Ur of the Chaldeans to give me this land to inherit forever, and so that I might establish a holy line: blessed be the Most High forever.”
He blessed Jacob and said, “My son, over whom I rejoice with all my heart and love, may your grace and mercy be lifted up on him and on his descendants always.

Do not abandon him or treat him as nothing from now on to the days of eternity, and may your eyes be opened on him and on his descendants, so that you will protect him, and bless him, and make him holy as a nation for your inheritance.

Bless him with all your blessings from now to all the days of eternity, and renew your covenant and your grace with him and with his descendants according to all your good pleasure through all the generations of the earth.”

notes.text: The text reads “forty-fourth jubilee … second year”; Charles read “forty-second … sixth.” Abraham died in 2109 from creation, at 175 (see 23:8). Feast of Weeks: the fifteenth of the third month, about June 5.
Compare Gen 27:29.
All the descendants of Seth: all humankind.
“Do not eat with them” was a key question in the time of the Maccabees (1 Macc 1:62–63; Dan 1:8).
“House” here means “family.”

chapters.heading: Abraham’s Last Feast, Prayer, and Blessing of Jacob

verses.text: He placed two of Jacob’s fingers on his eyes, and blessed the God of gods, and covered his face, stretched out his feet, slept the sleep of eternity, and was gathered to his fathers.
In spite of all this, Jacob lay in his bosom and did not know that his father’s father Abraham was dead.
Jacob woke from his sleep and found Abraham cold as ice, and said, “Father, father!” but no one answered, and he knew that he was dead.

He got up from his bosom and ran and told his mother Rebecca. Rebecca went to Isaac in the night and told him, and they went together, with Jacob, and a lamp in his hand, and when they went in they found Abraham lying dead.
Isaac fell on his father’s face and wept and kissed him.
The voices were heard in Abraham’s house, and his son Ishmael got up and went to his father Abraham and wept over him, he and the whole house of Abraham, and they wept with a great weeping.

His sons Isaac and Ishmael buried him in the double cave, near his wife Sarah, and they mourned him forty days, all the men of his house, Isaac and Ishmael and all their sons, and all the sons of Keturah in their places; and the days of weeping for Abraham ended.
He lived three jubilees and four weeks of years, a hundred and seventy-five years, and completed the days of his life, old and full of days.{a}

For the days of the forefathers’ lives were nineteen jubilees; and after the flood they began to be fewer than nineteen jubilees, and to shrink in jubilees, and to grow old quickly and be full of their days because of many troubles and the wickedness of their ways, except for Abraham.{b}

For Abraham was perfect in all his deeds with the Lord and pleasing in righteousness all the days of his life; yet he did not complete four jubilees in his life, when he had grown old because of the wickedness, and was full of his days.
Every generation arising between now and the great day of judgment will age rapidly, before reaching even two jubilees, and old age will strip away their understanding.
In those days, if a person lives a jubilee and a half of years, they will say of him, “He has lived long,” and most of his days are pain, sorrow, and trouble, with no peace.{c}

For calamity follows calamity, wound follows wound, trouble follows trouble, and bad news follows bad news, illness follows illness, and all such evil judgments one after another: illness and overthrow, snow, frost, and ice, fever, chills, numbness, famine, death, sword, captivity, and all kinds of calamities and pains.
All these will come on an evil generation that transgresses on the earth; their works are uncleanness and fornication, pollution and abominations.

Then they will say, “The days of the forefathers were many, even up to a thousand years, and were good; but see, the days of our life, if a person has lived long, are seventy years, or if he is strong, eighty, and those are evil, and there is no peace in the days of this evil generation.”{d}

In that generation the sons will convict their fathers and elders of sin and unrighteousness, of the words of their mouths and the great wickedness they commit, and of their abandoning the covenant that the Lord made between them and himself, that they should keep and do all his commandments, ordinances, and laws, without turning to the right or the left.
For all have done evil, every mouth speaks injustice, and all their works are uncleanness and abomination, and all their ways are pollution, uncleanness, and destruction.

The earth will be destroyed because of all their works; there will be no fruit of the vine and no oil, for their works are altogether faithless; and they will all perish together, animals, livestock, birds, and all the fish of the sea, because of human beings.

They will fight each other, the young against the old, the old against the young, the poor against the rich, the lowly against the great, the beggar against the prince, over the law and the covenant; for they have forgotten the commandment, the covenant, the feasts, the months, the sabbaths, the jubilees, and all judgments.
They will stand with bows, swords, and war to turn them back into the way, but they will not turn back until much blood has been shed on the earth, one by another.

The survivors will not turn back from their evil to the road of justice. All of them will puff themselves up with fraud and wealth, each seizing whatever belongs to his neighbor. They will invoke the great name, but not truthfully or justly, and will defile the most holy place with their impurity and the corruption of their pollution.
A great punishment will come on the deeds of this generation from the Lord, and he will hand them over to the sword, to judgment, to captivity, and to being plundered and devoured.

He will rouse the sinful nations against them, who have no mercy or compassion, and who will show favor to no one, old or young, for they are more wicked and strong to do evil than all humankind. They will use violence against Israel and transgression against Jacob, and much blood will be shed on the earth, and there will be none to gather the dead and none to bury them.
In those days they will cry aloud, and call and pray to be saved from the hand of the sinners, the Gentiles, but none will be saved.
The heads of the children will be white with gray hair, and a child of three weeks will look as old as a man of a hundred, and their stature will be destroyed by trouble and oppression.
In those days the children will begin to study the laws, to seek the commandments, and to return to the path of righteousness.{e}
The days will begin to grow many and increase among those human beings, until their days draw near a thousand years, and to a greater number of years than the number of days before.
There will be no old man, nor anyone who is not satisfied with his days, for all will be like children and youths.
They will complete all their days and live in peace and joy, and there will be no Satan nor any evil destroyer, for all their days will be days of blessing and healing.

In that time the Lord will heal his servants. They will get up and enjoy deep peace, and drive out their enemies. The righteous will see it and give thanks and be glad forever, watching all his judgments and curses fall on their foes.

Their bones will rest in the earth, and their spirits will have much joy, and they will know that it is the Lord who executes judgment and shows mercy to hundreds and thousands and to all who love him.
And you, Moses, write down these words; for so they are written and recorded on the heavenly tablets as a testimony for the generations forever.

notes.text: 3 × 49 + 4 × 7 = 175. The year was 2109 from creation.
Human life grows shorter as wickedness grows; compare 4 Ezra 5:50–55.
A jubilee and a half is 73½ years; compare Ps 90:10, “seventy years, or eighty if we are strong.”
A picture of the troubles of the early second century BC, most likely the Hellenizing crisis before and during the Maccabean revolt (1 Macc 1–2).

The text from here to verse 31 is a vision of a coming renewal. The people will not rise bodily; the righteous enjoy blessing while their bones rest in the earth and their spirits rejoice (verse 31), as in 1 Enoch 91–104. “Gray hair on the temples of the newborn” (verse 25) is also a sign of the end times in Sibylline Oracles 2.155.

chapters.heading: Abraham’s Death, Shorter Lives, and the Last Days

verses.text: After the death of Abraham the Lord blessed his son Isaac, and he left Hebron and went and lived at the Well of the Vision, in the first year of the third week of this jubilee, for seven years.{a}
A famine struck the land in the first year of the fourth week, a different one from the famine that came in Abraham’s time.

Jacob boiled lentil stew, and Esau came in from the field hungry. He said to his brother Jacob, “Give me some of this red stew.” Jacob said to him, “Sell me your birthright, and I will give you bread, and some of this lentil stew too.”
Esau said in his heart, “I am going to die; what good is this birthright to me?” and he said to Jacob, “I give it to you.”
Jacob said, “Swear to me today,” and he swore to him.

Jacob gave his brother Esau bread and stew, and he ate until he was full, and Esau despised his birthright; for this reason Esau’s name was called Edom, because of the red stew that Jacob gave him for his birthright.{b}
So Jacob became the elder and Esau was brought down from his rank.
The famine lay over the land, and in the second year of this week Isaac set out to go down to Egypt, and went to Abimelech, the king of the Philistines, at Gerar.
The Lord appeared to him and said, “Do not go down to Egypt. Live in the land that I will tell you about, and stay in this land, and I will be with you and bless you.

For to you and your descendants I will give all this land, and I will establish my oath that I swore to your father Abraham, and I will multiply your descendants like the stars of heaven, and give your descendants all this land.

In your descendants all the nations of the earth will be blessed, because your father obeyed my voice and kept my charge, my commandments, my laws, my ordinances, and my covenant; and now obey my voice and live in this land.”
He lived in Gerar for three weeks of years.{c}
Abimelech gave orders about him and about everything that was his, saying, “Any man who touches him or anything of his will surely die.”
Isaac grew strong among the Philistines and gained many possessions, cattle, sheep, camels, donkeys, and a large household.
He sowed in the land of the Philistines and harvested a hundredfold, and Isaac became very great, and the Philistines envied him.
Now all the wells that Abraham’s servants had dug in Abraham’s lifetime, the Philistines had stopped up after Abraham’s death and filled with earth.
Abimelech said to Isaac, “Leave us, for you are much stronger than we are,” and Isaac left there in the first year of the seventh week and stayed in the valleys of Gerar.

They dug again the wells of water that his father Abraham’s servants had dug and that the Philistines had closed after the death of his father Abraham, and he gave them the names that his father Abraham had given them.

Isaac’s servants dug a well in the valley and found living water, and the shepherds of Gerar quarreled with Isaac’s shepherds, saying, “The water is ours.” Isaac named the well “Perversity,” because they had been perverse with us.{d}

They dug a second well, and they quarreled over that one too, and he named it “Enmity.” He moved on from there and they dug another well, and over that one they did not quarrel, and he named it “Room.” Isaac said, “Now the Lord has made room for us, and we have increased in the land.”{e}
From there he went up to the Well of the Oath, in the first year of the first week in the forty-fourth jubilee.{f}

The Lord appeared to him that night, on the first day of the first month, and told him, “I am the God of your father Abraham. Do not fear, for I am with you. I will bless you and certainly make your descendants as many as the grains of earth’s sand, for my servant Abraham’s sake.”{g}
He built there an altar, which his father Abraham had first built, and he called on the name of the Lord, and offered sacrifice to the God of his father Abraham.
They dug a well and found living water.
Isaac’s servants dug another well but found no water. They went and told Isaac they had found none, and Isaac said, “I made an oath to the Philistines today, and so this has been brought upon us.”{h}
He named that place the Well of the Oath, for there he had sworn to Abimelech, to his friend Ahuzzath, and to Phicol the commander of his army.
Isaac knew that day that he had sworn to them under constraint, to make peace with them.

That day Isaac pronounced a curse: “Cursed be the Philistines until the day of wrath and fury, out of all the nations. May God make them a mockery and a curse, an object of rage and anger, in the hands of sinners, the Gentiles, and in the hands of the Kittim.{i}

Whoever escapes the sword of the enemy and the Kittim, may the righteous nation root out in judgment from under heaven; for they will be enemies and foes of my children through their generations on the earth.

No remnant will be left to them, and no one will be saved on the day of the wrath of judgment; for the whole seed of the Philistines is reserved for destruction, uprooting, and expulsion from the earth, and there will be left to these Caphtorim no name or descendants on the earth.{j}

Though he go up to heaven, he will be brought down from there; though he make himself strong on earth, he will be dragged out from there; though he hide among the nations, even from there he will be rooted out; though he go down to Sheol, there too his condemnation will be great, and there too he will have no peace.
If he goes into captivity, those who seek his life will kill him on the way, and neither name nor descendants will be left to him on all the earth, for he will depart into eternal curse.”
So it stands written about him on the heavenly tablets, to be carried out against him on the day of judgment, so that he will be uprooted from the earth.

notes.text: Beer-lahai-roi, “the well of the Living One who sees me” (Gen 25:11).
Edom means “red.”
Three weeks of years is twenty-one years. Charles’s chronology puts this in 2080–2101 from creation.
Hebrew Esek, “quarrel” (Gen 26:20).
Hebrew Sitnah, “enmity,” and Rehoboth, “open spaces” (Gen 26:21–22).
Beersheba, “well of the oath” or “of seven.”
The new moon of the first month is the first day of the first month, about March 22, a Wednesday in this calendar.
In the Hebrew of Gen 26:32 the servants say “we have found water”; the Greek reads as here. Here the failure to find water is read as a result of the oath made with Abimelech.

The curse reflects the bitterness toward the Philistines in the Maccabean period, in which their coastal cities were attacked and taken. Kittim: originally Cyprus; later the western powers, Greeks and Romans.
Caphtor, usually Crete, is named in Amos 9:7 as the Philistines’ origin.

chapters.heading: Isaac at the Well of Vision, Esau’s Birthright, and Gerar

verses.text: In the second year of this week of this jubilee, Rebecca summoned her son Jacob and told him, “My son, you must not marry one of the Canaanite women, as your brother Esau did. He married two of them, and they have made my life bitter with all their defiling ways. Everything they do is sexual immorality and lust, and nothing about them is just; their conduct is wicked.
I love you very much, my son, and my heart and my affection bless you every hour of the day and every watch of the night.

Now, my son, listen to my voice and do your mother’s will: do not take a wife from the daughters of this land, but only from the house of my father and from my father’s relatives. You will take a wife from the house of my father, and the Most High God will bless you, and your children will be a righteous generation and a holy line.”

Jacob said to his mother Rebecca, “Look, mother, I am nine weeks of years old, and I have not known nor touched any woman, nor have I betrothed myself to any, nor even thought of taking a wife from the daughters of Canaan.{a}
I remember, Mother, what our father Abraham told me: not to marry a Canaanite woman, but to choose a wife from my father’s house and from among my kin.
