I have heard before that daughters have been born to your brother Laban, and I have set my heart on them to take a wife from among them.
That is why I have kept watch over my spirit all my life, so that I do not sin or ruin any of my ways. Abraham my father gave me many commands about lust and sexual immorality.

In spite of all he commanded me, for these twenty-two years my brother has argued with me, speaking to me often and saying, ‘My brother, take a sister of my two wives as your wife,’ but I refuse to do as he has done.
Mother, I promise you that as long as I live I will never marry one of the Canaanite women, and I will not behave wickedly as my brother has.
Do not be afraid, mother; be assured that I will do your will and walk in uprightness, and never corrupt my ways.”
Then she raised her face toward heaven, spread out her fingers, and opening her mouth blessed God Most High, maker of heaven and earth, offering him thanks and praise.

She said, “Blessed be the Lord God, and may his holy name be blessed forever and ever, who has given me Jacob as a pure son and a holy line; for he is yours, and yours shall his descendants be continually and through all the generations forever.
Bless him, Lord, and put in my mouth the blessing of righteousness, so that I may bless him.”
At that hour, when the spirit of righteousness came down into her mouth, she placed both her hands on Jacob’s head and said,{b}

“Blessed are you, Lord of righteousness and God of the ages; may he bless you beyond all the generations of human beings. My son, may he give you the path of righteousness, and reveal righteousness to your descendants.

May he give you many sons in your lifetime; may they grow up as numerous as the months of the year; may their children be great and many, outnumbering the stars of heaven and the sand on the seashore.{c}
May he give them this good land, as he said he would give it to Abraham and his descendants after him always, and may they hold it as a possession forever.
May I see born to you, my son, blessed children during my life, and may all your descendants be a blessed and holy line.
As you have refreshed your mother’s spirit during your life, the womb of her who bore you blesses you, my affection and my breasts bless you, and my mouth and my tongue praise you greatly.
Increase and spread over the earth, and may your descendants be perfect in the joy of heaven and earth forever, and may your descendants rejoice, and on the great day of peace may they have peace.

May your name and your descendants last through all the ages, and may the Most High God be their God, and the God of righteousness live with them, and may his sanctuary be built by them through all the ages.
Blessed be the one who blesses you, and may all flesh that falsely curses you be cursed.”
She kissed him and said, “May the Lord of the world love you as the heart of your mother and her affection rejoice in you and bless you.” And she stopped blessing.

notes.text: Nine weeks of years is 63. Genesis 25:26 says he was 60 at the twins’ birth and does not give his age at the blessing; Jubilees counts his age by its own scheme.
Some manuscripts read “Holy Spirit” here.
Twelve sons, the twelve months of the year.

chapters.heading: Rebecca Warns Jacob and Blesses Him

verses.text: In the seventh year of this week Isaac called his elder son Esau and said to him, “I am old, my son, and see, my eyes are dim, and I do not know the day of my death.

Now take your hunting weapons, your quiver and bow, and go out to the field, and hunt and catch some game for me, my son, and make me tasty food, such as my soul loves, and bring it to me to eat, so that my soul may bless you before I die.”
But Rebecca heard Isaac speaking to Esau.
Esau went out early to the field to hunt and catch game and bring it home to his father.

Rebecca called her son Jacob and said to him, “Look, I heard your father Isaac speaking to your brother Esau, saying, ‘Hunt for me, and make me tasty food, and bring it to me so that I may eat and bless you before the Lord before I die.’

Now, my son, obey my voice in what I command you: go to your flock and bring me two good kids of the goats, and I will make them into tasty food for your father, such as he loves, and you will bring it to your father so that he may eat and bless you before the Lord before he dies, and so that you may be blessed.”
Jacob said to his mother Rebecca, “Mother, I will not hold back anything my father would eat and that would please him. I only fear, mother, that he will recognize my voice and want to touch me.

You know that I am smooth and my brother Esau is hairy, and I will look to his eyes like a wrongdoer, and do something he did not command me, and he will be angry with me, and I will bring on myself a curse and not a blessing.”
His mother Rebecca said to him, “Let your curse be on me, my son; only obey my voice.”
Jacob did as his mother Rebecca told him. He went and fetched two fine, fat young goats and brought them to his mother, who prepared them as a savory dish, just the way his father loved it.

Rebecca took the good clothes of her elder son Esau, which were with her in the house, and dressed her younger son Jacob in them, and put the skins of the kids on his hands and on the bare parts of his neck.
She gave the food and the bread she had prepared into the hand of her son Jacob.
Jacob went in to his father and said, “I am your son; I have done as you told me. Get up, sit, and eat what I have caught, father, so that your soul may bless me.”
Isaac said to his son, “How did you find it so quickly, my son?”
Jacob said, “Because the Lord your God let me find it.”
Isaac said to him, “Come near, so that I may feel you, my son, to see whether you are my son Esau or not.”
Jacob went near to his father Isaac, and he felt him, and said,

“The voice is Jacob’s voice, but the hands are the hands of Esau,” and he did not recognize him, because it was a turn of events from heaven to take away his power of perception, and Isaac did not recognize him, for his hands were hairy like his brother Esau’s, so that he blessed him.{a}
He said, “Are you my son Esau?” and he said, “I am your son.” He said, “Bring it near to me so that I may eat of what you have caught, my son, so that my soul may bless you.”
He brought it near to him and he ate, and he brought him wine and he drank.
His father Isaac said to him, “Come near and kiss me, my son.” He came near and kissed him.
He smelled the smell of his clothes, and he blessed him and said, “Look, the smell of my son is like the smell of a full field that the Lord has blessed.
May the Lord give you of the dew of heaven and of the dew of the earth, and plenty of grain and oil. Let nations serve you, and peoples bow down to you.

Be lord over your brothers, and let your mother’s sons bow down to you; and may all the blessings with which the Lord has blessed me and blessed my father Abraham be given to you and your descendants forever. Cursed be anyone who curses you, and blessed be anyone who blesses you.”
As soon as Isaac had finished blessing his son Jacob, and Jacob had gone out from his father Isaac, he hid himself, and his brother Esau came in from his hunting.
He also made tasty food and brought it to his father, and said to his father, “Let my father get up and eat of my game, so that your soul may bless me.”
His father Isaac said to him, “Who are you?” and he said to him, “I am your firstborn, your son Esau; I have done as you commanded me.”

Isaac was greatly astonished and said, “Who is the one who hunted and caught game and brought it to me, and I ate everything before you came, and blessed him? He will be blessed, and all his descendants forever.”
When Esau heard his father Isaac’s words, he cried out with a very loud and bitter cry and said to his father, “Bless me, me also, father.”

He said to him, “Your brother came with deceit and has taken away your blessing.” Esau said, “Now I know why his name is Jacob: look, he has supplanted me these two times; he took away my birthright, and now he has taken my blessing.”{b}

He said, “Have you not kept a blessing for me, father?” Isaac answered Esau, “Look, I have made him your lord, and I have given all his brothers to him as servants, and I have strengthened him with plenty of grain, wine, and oil; and what can I do now for you, my son?”
Esau said to his father Isaac, “Do you have only one blessing, father? Bless me, me also, father.” And Esau lifted up his voice and wept.
Isaac answered and said to him, “Look, your dwelling will be far from the dew of the earth and far from the dew of heaven above.

By your sword you will live, and you will serve your brother. When you grow great and shake his yoke from your neck, you will sin a complete sin to death, and your descendants will be rooted out from under heaven.”{c}
Esau kept menacing Jacob over the blessing his father had given him. He said to himself, “Let the days of mourning for my father come soon, so that I can kill my brother Jacob.”

notes.text: “Dispensation from heaven” excuses the deception: as with Jacob’s deceit in Genesis, the book makes God the author of it.
Jacob means “he grasps the heel” and so “he supplants” (Gen 27:36).
This line departs from Genesis 27:40, which says only that Esau will break the yoke. Here breaking it is a sin that destroys Edom, which fits the second-century BC hostility to Edom.

chapters.heading: Jacob Obtains the Firstborn’s Blessing

verses.text: Esau’s words were told to Rebecca in a dream, and Rebecca sent and called her younger son Jacob and said to him,
“Look, your brother Esau will take revenge on you and kill you.

So now, my son, obey my voice, and get up and flee to my brother Laban in Haran, and stay with him a few days until your brother’s anger turns away and he lets go of his anger against you and forgets everything you have done; then I will send and bring you back from there.”
Jacob said, “I am not afraid; if he wants to kill me, I will kill him.”
But she said to him, “Let me not lose both my sons in one day.”

Jacob said to his mother Rebecca, “You know my father is old and cannot see, because his eyes are dim. If I leave him, it will seem wrong to him, for I would be going away from you, and my father will be angry and curse me. I will not go. When he sends me himself, then I will.”{a}
Rebecca said to Jacob, “I will go in and talk with him, and he will send you off.”

Rebecca went in and said to Isaac, “I am weary of my life because of the two daughters of Heth whom Esau has taken as wives; and if Jacob takes a wife from among the daughters of the land such as these, what is the point of my living any longer? For the daughters of Canaan are evil.”
Isaac called Jacob and blessed him, and warned him, and said to him,

“Do not take a wife from any of the daughters of Canaan; get up and go to Mesopotamia, to the house of Bethuel, your mother’s father, and take a wife from there from the daughters of Laban, your mother’s brother.

May God Almighty bless you and increase and multiply you, so that you become a company of nations, and give you the blessings of my father Abraham, to you and your descendants after you, so that you may inherit the land of your wanderings and all the land God gave to Abraham. Go, my son, in peace.”
Isaac sent Jacob away, and he went to Mesopotamia, to Laban, son of Bethuel the Syrian, brother of Rebecca, Jacob’s mother.
After Jacob had set out for Mesopotamia, Rebecca’s spirit grieved for her son, and she wept.
Isaac said to Rebecca, “My sister, do not weep because of my son Jacob; for he goes in peace and will return in peace.{b}
The Most High God will keep him from all evil and will be with him, for he will not abandon him all his days.
For I know that his ways will prosper in all things wherever he goes, until he returns to us in peace and we see him in peace.
Do not fear for him, my sister. He walks a straight road, a man of integrity and faithfulness; he will not be lost. Do not cry.”
Isaac comforted Rebecca over her son Jacob and blessed him.

In the first year of the second week of the forty-fourth jubilee, Jacob left the Well of the Oath for Haran. On the first day of the first month of that week he reached Luz in the hills, which is Bethel. He arrived there in the evening, left the road toward the west that night, and slept there, since the sun had gone down.{c}
He took one of the stones of that place and laid it under the tree at his head, and he was traveling alone, and he slept.
That night he dreamed, and a ladder was set up on the earth, and its top reached to heaven, and the angels of the Lord went up and down on it, and the Lord stood on it.
He spoke to Jacob and said, “I am the Lord, God of your father Abraham and God of Isaac; the land you are sleeping on I will give to you and your descendants after you.
Your descendants will be like the dust of the earth, and you will spread to the west and east, north and south, and in you and your descendants all the families of the nations will be blessed.
Look, I will be with you, and will keep you wherever you go, and I will bring you back to this land in peace; for I will not leave you until I do everything I told you.”

Jacob woke from his sleep and said, “This place is really the house of the Lord, and I never knew.” Afraid, he said, “This place is awe-inspiring. It is none other than God’s house, and this is the gate of heaven.”
Early in the morning Jacob rose, took the stone that had been under his head, stood it up as a marker, and poured oil over its top. He named the place Bethel; its earlier name was Luz.

Jacob made a vow to the Lord, saying, “If the Lord is with me and keeps me on this way I am going, and gives me bread to eat and clothes to wear, so that I come back to my father’s house in peace, then the Lord will be my God, and this stone that I have set up as a pillar for a sign in this place will be the Lord’s house, and of all that you give me I will give the tenth to you, my God.”

notes.text: The author wants to clear Jacob of leaving his aged father.
“Sister” as an affectionate name for a wife is found in Tobit 5:20 and Song of Songs 4:9. Here it also defends Isaac’s calling Rebecca his sister at Gerar.
The first day of the first month is about March 22, a Wednesday. The year is 2115 from creation in Charles’s count. Luz is the old name for Bethel.

chapters.heading: Jacob Sent to Mesopotamia; the Dream at Bethel

verses.text: He went on his journey and came to the land of the east, to Laban, Rebecca’s brother, and stayed with him, and served him for his daughter Rachel for one week of years.{a}
In the first year of the third week he said to him, “Give me my wife, for whom I have served you seven years,” and Laban said to Jacob, “I will give you your wife.”
Laban made a feast and took his elder daughter Leah and gave her to Jacob as a wife, and gave her his maid Zilpah as her maid; and Jacob did not know, for he thought she was Rachel.

He went in to her, and it was Leah; and Jacob was angry with Laban and said to him, “Why have you done this to me? Did I not serve you for Rachel and not for Leah? Why have you wronged me? Take your daughter and I will go, for you have done evil to me.”
For Jacob loved Rachel more than Leah, because Leah’s eyes were weak, but her figure was very handsome; but Rachel had beautiful eyes and a beautiful and very handsome figure.

Laban said to Jacob, “It is not done this way in our country, to give the younger before the elder.” And it is not right to do this; for it is ordained and written on the heavenly tablets that no one should give his younger daughter before the elder; the elder is given first and the younger after her; and the man who does this, they record guilt against him in heaven, and no one who does this is righteous, for this deed is evil before the Lord.{b}
Command the children of Israel not to do this: let them not take or give the younger before they have given the elder, for it is very wicked.

Laban said to Jacob, “Let the seven days of the feast for this one pass, and I will give you Rachel, so that you will serve me another seven years, and pasture my sheep as you did in the former week.”
On the day when the seven days of Leah’s feast had passed, Laban gave Rachel to Jacob, so that he would serve him another seven years, and he gave Rachel Bilhah, the sister of Zilpah, as a maid.{c}
He served another seven years for Rachel, for Leah had been given to him for nothing.
The Lord opened Leah’s womb. She conceived and bore Jacob a son, whom he named Reuben, on the fourteenth of the ninth month, in the first year of the third week.{d}
But Rachel’s womb was closed, for the Lord saw that Leah was hated and Rachel loved.
Again Jacob went in to Leah, and she conceived and bore Jacob a second son, and he named him Simeon, on the twenty-first of the tenth month, in the third year of this week.{e}
Again Jacob went in to Leah, and she conceived and bore a third son, and he named him Levi, on the new moon of the first month, in the sixth year of this week.{f}
Jacob slept with her again. She conceived and bore a fourth son, whom he named Judah, on the fifteenth of the third month, in the first year of the fourth week.{g}
Rachel was jealous of Leah because of all this, since she had no children. She said to Jacob, “Give me children.” Jacob replied, “Have I kept the fruit of the womb from you? Have I left you?”
When Rachel saw that Leah had borne Jacob four sons, Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and Judah, she said to him, “Go in to my maid Bilhah, and she will conceive and bear a son for me.”
She gave him her maid Bilhah as a wife. He went in to her, and she conceived and bore him a son, and he named him Dan, on the ninth of the sixth month, in the sixth year of the third week.{h}
Jacob slept with Bilhah a second time. She conceived and bore Jacob another son, whom Rachel named Naphtali, on the fifth of the seventh month, in the second year of the fourth week.{i}

When Leah realized she had stopped bearing children, she grew envious of Rachel and gave her own servant Zilpah to Jacob as a wife. Zilpah conceived and bore a son, whom Leah named Gad, on the twelfth of the eighth month, in the third year of the fourth week.{j}
He went in to her again, and she conceived and bore him a second son, and Leah named him Asher, on the second of the eleventh month, in the fifth year of the fourth week.{k}
Jacob slept with Leah, who conceived and gave birth to a son, Issachar, on the fourth day of the fifth month in the fourth year of the fourth week; she handed him over to a wet-nurse.{l}

Jacob went in again to her, and she conceived and bore two children, a son and a daughter, and she named the son Zebulun and the daughter Dinah, on the seventh of the seventh month, in the sixth year of the fourth week.{m}
The Lord was gracious to Rachel and opened her womb, and she conceived and bore a son, and she named him Joseph, on the new moon of the fourth month, in the sixth year of this fourth week.{n}

In the days when Joseph was born, Jacob said to Laban, “Give me my wives and sons, and let me go to my father Isaac and build myself a house; for I have completed the years I served you for your two daughters, and I will go to my father’s house.”
Laban said to Jacob, “Stay with me for your wages, and pasture my flock for me again, and take your wages.”
They agreed with each other that he would give him as his wages the lambs and kids born black, spotted, and white; these were to be his wages.
All the sheep bore spotted, speckled, and black young, variously marked, and they bore again lambs like themselves, and all that were spotted were Jacob’s and those not spotted were Laban’s.
Jacob’s possessions multiplied greatly, and he had cattle, sheep, donkeys, camels, menservants, and maidservants.
Laban and his sons envied Jacob, and Laban took his sheep back from him, and watched him with evil intent.

notes.text: Seven years.
This verse is the angel’s comment. The rule is not known elsewhere in Jewish tradition.
The Law forbids marrying two living sisters (Lev 18:18). Bilhah and Zilpah are sisters here and in the Testament of Naphtali 1; later Jewish tradition makes them Laban’s daughters.
Reuben means “See, a son.” The ninth month, day 14, falls about December 2. The year is 2122 from creation in Charles’s count.
Tenth month, day 21: about January 9. Simeon means “hearing.”
First day of the first month: about March 22, a Wednesday. Levi means “joined.”
Third month, day 15: about early June, the Feast of Weeks. Judah means “praise.” The year number in the manuscripts is uncertain.
Sixth month, day 9: about August 28. Dan means “he judged.” The year number is uncertain in the manuscripts.
Seventh month, day 5: about September 24. Naphtali means “my wrestling.”
Eighth month, day 12: about October 31. Gad means “fortune.”
Eleventh month, day 2: about January 20. Asher means “happy.”
Fifth month, day 4: about July 24. Issachar means “wages.” The order of births is disputed in the manuscripts.
Seventh month, day 7: about September 26.

First day of the fourth month: about June 21. The year is 2134 from creation in Charles’s count. Joseph means “may he add.” The twelve sons follow the order of Genesis 29–35: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Dan, Naphtali, Gad, Asher, Issachar, Zebulun, Joseph, Benjamin.

chapters.heading: Jacob’s Marriages and the Birth of His Children

verses.text: When Rachel had borne Joseph, Laban went to shear his sheep, for they were a three days’ journey from him.
Jacob saw that Laban was going to shear his sheep, and he called Leah and Rachel and spoke kindly to them, that they should come with him to the land of Canaan.
For he told them how he had seen everything in a dream, everything that God had said to him about returning to his father’s house, and they said, “We will go with you to every place where you go.”

Jacob blessed the God of his father Isaac and the God of his grandfather Abraham. He rose, seated his wives and children on camels, gathered all his goods, crossed the river, and entered Gilead. He concealed his plan from Laban and told him nothing.

In the seventh year of the fourth week, on the twenty-first of the first month, Jacob set out toward Gilead. Laban chased after him and caught up with him in the hill country of Gilead, on the thirteenth of the third month.{a}
The Lord did not let him harm Jacob, for he appeared to him in a dream by night. And Laban spoke to Jacob.

On the fifteenth of those days Jacob made a feast for Laban and all who came with him, and Jacob swore to Laban that day, and Laban also to Jacob, that neither would cross the mountain of Gilead to the other with evil purpose.{b}
He made a heap there as a witness; for this reason the name of that place is called “The Heap of Witness,” after this heap.{c}
Before that, however, Gilead was known as the land of the Rephaim, since the Rephaim were born there: giants ten cubits tall, or nine, or eight, down to seven.{d}
Their territory stretched from the land of the Ammonites to Mount Hermon, and the seats of their kingdom were Karnaim, Ashtaroth, Edrei, Misur, and Beon.{e}

The Lord wiped them out for the wickedness of their deeds, for they were thoroughly vicious. The Amorites, wicked and sinful, settled in their place, and today no nation has filled up its sins to the same extent; none of them has a long life on the earth anymore.
Jacob sent Laban away, and he went to Mesopotamia, the land of the east, and Jacob returned to the land of Gilead.

He crossed the Jabbok in the ninth month, on the eleventh of it. On that day his brother Esau came to him, and he was reconciled to him, and Esau left him for the land of Seir, but Jacob lived in tents.{f}

In the first year of the fifth week in this jubilee he crossed the Jordan and lived beyond the Jordan, and he pastured his sheep from the Sea of the Heap to Beth-shan, to Dothan, and to the forest of Akrabbim.{g}
He sent to his father Isaac from all his goods clothing, food, meat, drink, milk, butter, cheese, and some dates of the valley,

and also to his mother Rebecca four times a year, at the turning points of the months, between plowing and harvest, between late summer and the rains, and between winter and spring, at Abraham’s tower.{h}
Isaac had come back from Beer-sheba, the Well of the Oath, and gone up to his father Abraham’s tower, where he was living by himself, away from Esau his son.

For in the days when Jacob went to Mesopotamia, Esau took as a wife Mahalath, the daughter of Ishmael, and he gathered all his father’s flocks and his wives and went up and lived on Mount Seir, and left his father Isaac alone at the Well of the Oath.
Isaac went up from the Well of the Oath and lived in the tower of his father Abraham in the mountains of Hebron.
Jacob sent there everything he used to send his father and mother from time to time, whatever they needed. They blessed Jacob with their whole heart and soul.

notes.text: First month, day 21: about April 11. Third month, day 13: about June 2.
The fifteenth of the third month, the Feast of Weeks, about June 4.
Gilead, in Hebrew Galeed, means “heap of witness” (Gen 31:47).
Ten cubits is about 15 feet (4.5 m); seven cubits about 10½ feet (3.2 m); the cubit is taken as 18 inches. Compare Gen 14:5; Deut 3:11.
These places were scenes of Judas Maccabeus’s victories (1 Macc 5), which may be why they are named.
Ninth month, day 11: about November 29.
Year 2136 from creation in Charles’s count. The text of the first place name is damaged; a Latin copy has “from the Salt Sea.”
The four times match the four quarters of the 364-day year, each ending with a short day, the “days of remembrance” at the turn of the seasons.

chapters.heading: Jacob’s Flight and Covenant with Laban

verses.text: In the first year of the sixth week he went up to Salem, east of Shechem, in peace, in the fourth month.{a}
They took Dinah, Jacob’s daughter, into the house of Shechem, the son of Hamor the Hivite, ruler of the region. He raped and defiled her. She was a young girl of twelve.

He begged his father and her brothers to give her to him as a wife. Jacob and his sons were angry at the men of Shechem, for they had defiled their sister Dinah, and they spoke to them with evil intent and dealt deceitfully with them and tricked them.{b}

Simeon and Levi came unexpectedly to Shechem and carried out judgment on all the men of Shechem, and killed all the men they found in it and left not one remaining; they killed them all in torment, because they had dishonored their sister Dinah.

Never again must it happen, from this day on, that a daughter of Israel is violated. Judgment has been decreed in heaven against such people: that every Shechemite man be put to the sword, because they committed an outrage in Israel.

The Lord delivered them into the hands of the sons of Jacob to wipe them out with the sword and carry out judgment on them, so that it would not be done again in Israel that a virgin of Israel is defiled.

If there is anyone in Israel who wants to give his daughter or his sister to a man of the descendants of the Gentiles, he will surely die, and they will stone him; for he has done a shameful thing in Israel; and they will burn the woman with fire, because she has dishonored the name of her father’s house, and she will be rooted out of Israel.{c}

Let no adulteress and no uncleanness be found in Israel through all the days of the generations of the earth; for Israel is holy to the Lord, and every man who has defiled it will surely die; they will stone him.
For so it has been ordained and written on the heavenly tablets about all the descendants of Israel: whoever defiles it will surely die, and will be stoned.

To this law there is no limit of days, and no remission, and no atonement; but the man who has defiled his daughter will be rooted out from all Israel, because he has given some of his seed to Moloch and acted impiously, defiling it.{d}

You, Moses, command the children of Israel and warn them not to give their daughters to the Gentiles, and not to take any of the Gentiles’ daughters for their sons, for this is abominable before the Lord.

For this reason I have written for you in the words of the Law all the deeds of the Shechemites against Dinah, and how Jacob’s sons said, “We will not give our daughter to a man who is uncircumcised, for that would be a disgrace to us.”
It is a shame for Israel, both for those who give and for those who take foreign women, for this is defiling and loathsome to Israel.
Israel will not be free of this uncleanness if it has a wife from the daughters of the Gentiles, or has given any of its daughters to a man of any of the Gentiles.

Plague will follow plague and curse follow curse, and every kind of judgment will fall on anyone who does this, or who looks away from people practicing such impurity, or from those who pollute the Lord’s sanctuary or dishonor his holy name. Then the entire nation will be judged together for this one man’s impurity and profanation.

There will be no favoritism and no partiality, and he will not accept from his hands fruits, offerings, burnt offerings, fat, or the fragrance of a pleasing aroma, so as to accept it; and so it will be with every man or woman in Israel who defiles the sanctuary.

That is why I ordered you: “Give this witness to Israel. Look at what became of the Shechemites and their sons: two of Jacob’s sons handed them over to death, and killed them in torment. It was credited to the two as justice, and recorded in their favor as justice.

The descendants of Levi were chosen for the priesthood and to be Levites, to serve before the Lord continually, as we do, and so that Levi and his sons may be blessed forever; for he was zealous to carry out righteousness, judgment, and vengeance on all who rose up against Israel.{e}
So they record on the heavenly tablets blessing and righteousness in his favor before the God of all.

We recall the man’s justice, shown throughout his life in every season. For a thousand generations they will keep the record, and it will pass to him and to his descendants after him. He is entered on the heavenly tablets as a friend and a just man.

All this account I have written for you, and have commanded you to tell the children of Israel that they should not sin, nor transgress the ordinances, nor break the covenant that has been ordained for them, but should fulfill it and be recorded as friends.

But if they transgress and practice uncleanness in any way, they will be recorded on the heavenly tablets as adversaries, and they will be destroyed out of the book of life, and they will be recorded in the book of those who will be destroyed and rooted out of the earth.{f}

On the day when the sons of Jacob killed Shechem, a writing was recorded in their favor in heaven, that they had executed righteousness, uprightness, and vengeance on the sinners, and it was written for a blessing.

They brought their sister Dinah out of Shechem’s house, and they took captive everything in Shechem, their sheep, cattle, donkeys, all their wealth, and all their flocks, and brought them all to their father Jacob.
He reproached them because they had put the city to the sword, for he feared those who lived in the land, the Canaanites and the Perizzites.
The dread of the Lord was on all the cities around Shechem, and they did not rise to pursue the sons of Jacob, for terror had fallen on them.

notes.text: Charles dates this to 2143 from creation. “Salem” and “in peace” are the same Hebrew word, shalem/shalom, and the text joins both readings (Gen 33:18). The fourth month runs from about June 21.

The book leaves out the circumcision of the Shechemites, for it approves of what Simeon and Levi did and praises it. Genesis 49:5–7 condemns their act. The attitude here fits the strong hostility to Shechem (the Samaritans) in the author’s time.
This passage is a fierce attack on marriage with outsiders. Leviticus 21:9 prescribes burning only for a priest’s daughter who becomes a prostitute.
Compare Lev 18:21 and 20:2–5, where giving offspring to Moloch is forbidden. Here marrying a daughter to a Gentile is made the same as that sin.
Another reason for Levi’s choice is given in 32:3. Compare Testament of Levi 4–6.
The “book of life” (Ex 32:32; Ps 69:28) first meant the register of the living people of God. Later it means eternal life (Rev 3:5; 1 Enoch 47:3).

chapters.heading: Dinah, the Shechemites, and the Choice of Levi

verses.text: On the new moon of the month Jacob spoke to all the people of his house, saying, “Purify yourselves and change your clothes, and let us get up and go to Bethel, where I made a vow to him on the day I fled from my brother Esau, because he has been with me and brought me into this land in peace; and put away the foreign gods that are among you.”

They gave up the foreign gods and what was in their ears and on their necks, and Rachel gave Jacob all the idols she had stolen from her brother Laban. He burned them and broke them to pieces and destroyed them, and hid them under an oak in the land of Shechem.

He went up to Bethel on the new moon of the seventh month. He built an altar at the place where he had slept, and set up a pillar there, and sent word to his father Isaac to come to him for his sacrifice, and to his mother Rebecca.{a}
Isaac said, “Let my son Jacob come, and let me see him before I die.”

Jacob went to his father Isaac and his mother Rebecca, to the house of his father Abraham, and he took two of his sons with him, Levi and Judah, and he came to his father Isaac and his mother Rebecca.{b}
Rebecca came out of the tower to its entrance to kiss and hug Jacob. When she heard, “Your son Jacob is here,” her spirit had come back to life, and she kissed him.

She looked at his two sons and knew them, and she said, “Are these your sons, my son?” She hugged and kissed them and blessed them: “Through you Abraham’s descendants will become renowned, and you will be a blessing on the earth.”

Jacob went in to his father Isaac, to the room where he lay, and his two sons were with him, and he took his father’s hand and bent down and kissed him, and Isaac clung to the neck of his son Jacob and wept on his neck.
The dimness lifted from Isaac’s eyes and he saw Jacob’s two sons, Levi and Judah. He said, “Are these your sons, my son? They look just like you.”
Jacob told him that they were truly his sons; “and you have truly seen that they are truly my sons.”
They stepped up to him, and he turned, kissed them, and held them both in one embrace.
The spirit of prophecy fell on his lips. He took Levi’s right hand and Judah’s left.
He turned to Levi first, and began to bless him first, and said to him, “May the God of all, the very Lord of all the ages, bless you and your children through all the ages.{c}

May the Lord give you and your offspring great honor and splendor, and choose you and your offspring out of all humanity to come near him and serve in his sanctuary, like the angels of the presence and the holy ones. As they are, so may the descendants of your sons be: glorious, great, and holy, and may he make them great for all ages.{d}

They will be rulers, judges, and leaders over all the offspring of Jacob’s sons. They will speak the Lord’s word with justice and decide all his cases justly. They will make my ways known to Jacob and my paths to Israel. The Lord’s blessing will be placed in their mouths, to bless all the offspring of the beloved.{e}

Your mother named you Levi, and she named you rightly: you will be joined to the Lord and be a companion to all Jacob’s sons. Let his table be yours; eat from it, you and your sons. May your table be full in every generation, and your food never run short through all the ages.{f}
Let all who hate you fall down before you, let all your adversaries be rooted out and perish; blessed be the one who blesses you, and cursed be every nation that curses you.”

To Judah he said, “May the Lord give you strength and power to tread down all who hate you. You will be a prince, you and one of your sons, over the sons of Jacob; may your name and your sons’ name go out and cross every land and region. Then the Gentiles will fear before your face, and all the nations will quake, and all the peoples will tremble.
In you will be the help of Jacob, and in you will be found the salvation of Israel.

When you sit on the throne of the honor of your righteousness, there will be great peace for all the descendants of the sons of the beloved; blessed be the one who blesses you, and all who hate you, afflict you, and curse you will be rooted out and destroyed from the earth and be accursed.”
Turning, he kissed him again and embraced him, and rejoiced greatly because he had seen the sons of his son Jacob in very truth.
He went out from between his feet and fell down and bowed to him. And he blessed them. And Jacob rested there with his father Isaac that night, and they ate and drank with joy.
He made the two sons of Jacob sleep, one at his right hand and the other at his left, and it was counted to him as righteousness.
Through that night Jacob told his father everything: the great kindness the Lord had shown him, how he had made all his undertakings succeed, and guarded him from every harm.
Isaac blessed the God of his father Abraham, who had not withdrawn his mercy and righteousness from the sons of his servant Isaac.

In the morning Jacob told his father Isaac the vow he had made to the Lord, and the vision he had seen, and that he had built an altar, and that everything was ready for the sacrifice to be made before the Lord as he had vowed, and that he had come to set him on a donkey.

Isaac said to his son Jacob, “I cannot go with you, for I am old and cannot bear the journey. Go, my son, in peace, for I am a hundred and sixty-five years old this day; I can no longer travel. Set your mother on a donkey and let her go with you.{g}
I know, my son, that you have come on my account, and may this day be blessed on which you saw me alive and I also saw you, my son.

May you prosper and fulfill the vow you made; do not put off your vow, for you will be called to account for it; so make haste to carry it out, and may he who made all things be pleased, to whom you made the vow.”
He said to Rebecca, “Go with your son Jacob,” and Rebecca went with her son Jacob, and Deborah with her, and they came to Bethel.
Jacob remembered the prayer with which his father had blessed him and his sons Levi and Judah. He was glad and blessed the God of his fathers, Abraham and Isaac.

He said, “Now I know that I and my sons have an everlasting hope before the God of all.” So this was decreed for the two of them, and the way Isaac blessed them is written on the heavenly tablets as their lasting witness.

notes.text: The new moon of the seventh month is the first day of the seventh month, about September 20, a Wednesday.
Hebron. Rabbinic tradition does not mention this last meeting of Jacob and Isaac.
Levi is given first place. Compare Testament of Levi 9.
Levi’s line is to serve in the sanctuary as the two highest orders of angels serve in heaven (see 2:2, 18).
Priests who also rule: the Maccabean priest-princes held both roles. The beloved is Abraham.
Levi means “joined” (Gen 29:34).
Isaac was 60 when Jacob was born (Gen 25:26) and would be 165 at the time given here, which is about 105 years old when Jacob was 45; the book’s own count is meant.

chapters.heading: Jacob at Bethel and Hebron; Isaac Blesses Levi and Judah

verses.text: He stayed that night at Bethel, and Levi dreamed that they had ordained him and made him priest of the Most High God, him and his sons forever; and he woke from his sleep and blessed the Lord.{a}

Jacob got up early in the morning on the fourteenth of this month and gave a tithe of everything that came with him, of both people and cattle, of gold and every vessel and garment; yes, he gave tithes of everything.{b}

In those days Rachel became pregnant with her son Benjamin. Jacob counted his sons from him upward, and Levi fell to the portion of the Lord, and his father clothed him in the garments of the priesthood and filled his hands.{c}

On the fifteenth of this month he brought fourteen bulls from the herd, twenty-eight rams, forty-nine sheep, seven lambs, and twenty-one young goats to the altar as a burnt offering, a sweet aroma pleasing to God.{d}
This was his offering, because of the vow he had made that he would give a tenth, with their grain offerings and drink offerings.

When the fire had consumed it, he burned incense on the fire over it, and for a thank offering two oxen, four rams, four sheep, four male goats, two yearling sheep, and two kids of the goats; and so he did daily for seven days.
He and all his sons and his men ate this with joy there for seven days, blessing and thanking the Lord, who had delivered him from all his trouble and given him his vow.
He tithed all the clean animals and made a burnt sacrifice, but the unclean animals he did not give to his son Levi; and he gave him all the souls of the men.{e}

Levi served as priest at Bethel before his father Jacob, in preference to his ten brothers, and he was priest there, and Jacob fulfilled his vow; so he tithed again the tithe to the Lord and made it holy, and it became holy to him.

For this reason it is ordained on the heavenly tablets as a law that the tithe be tithed again, to eat before the Lord from year to year in the place chosen for his name to dwell, and to this law there is no limit of days forever.{f}

This ordinance is written so that it may be fulfilled from year to year, eating the second tithe before the Lord in the place chosen, and nothing is to remain over from it from this year to the year following.
For in its own year the seed is to be eaten until the days of the gathering of the year’s seed, and the wine until the days of the wine, and the oil until the days of its season.
All that is left over and has become old is to be treated as polluted; let it be burned with fire, for it is unclean.
So let them eat it together in the sanctuary, and not let it become old.

All the tithes of the cattle and sheep will be holy to the Lord, and will belong to his priests, who will eat them before him from year to year; for so it is ordained and engraved regarding the tithe on the heavenly tablets.

On the following night, the twenty-second day of this month, Jacob decided to build that place and surround the court with a wall, and to make it holy forever, for himself and his children after him.{g}
The Lord appeared to him by night and blessed him and said to him, “Your name will not be called Jacob, but they will name you Israel.”

He said to him again, “I am the Lord, who created heaven and earth, and I will increase you and multiply you greatly, and kings will come from you, and they will judge everywhere the foot of human beings has trodden.

I will give your descendants all the earth that is under heaven, and they will judge all the nations as they desire, and after that they will take possession of the whole earth and inherit it forever.”{h}
He finished speaking with him, and he went up from him, and Jacob watched until he had ascended into heaven.

He saw in a vision of the night, and an angel came down from heaven with seven tablets in his hands, and gave them to Jacob, and he read them and knew everything written in them that would happen to him and his sons through all the ages.{i}

He showed him all that was written on the tablets, and said to him, “Do not build this place, and do not make it an eternal sanctuary, and do not live here, for this is not the place. Go to the house of your father Abraham and live with your father Isaac until the day of your father’s death.{j}
For in Egypt you will die in peace, and in this land you will be buried with honor in the tomb of your fathers, with Abraham and Isaac.
Do not be afraid, for what you have seen and read will all be so; and write down everything as you have seen and read it.”
Jacob said, “Lord, how can I remember everything I have read and seen?” and he said to him, “I will bring everything to your remembrance.”{k}
He went up from him, and Jacob woke from his sleep and remembered everything he had read and seen, and he wrote down all the words he had read and seen.

He celebrated there yet another day, and sacrificed on it according to everything he had sacrificed on the former days, and he named it “Addition,” because this day was added, and the former days he called “The Feast.”{l}
So the right way was shown to him, and it stands written on the heavenly tablets; and it was revealed to him that he should keep it, adding this day to the seven days of the feast.
Its name was called “Addition,” because it was recorded among the feast days in the number of the days of the year.{m}

That night, the twenty-third of the month, Deborah, Rebecca’s nurse, died. She was buried beneath the town under the river oak. Jacob called the spot “The River of Deborah” and the oak “The Oak of Deborah’s Mourning.”{n}
Rebecca went back to her home, to his father Isaac. Jacob sent along with her rams, sheep, and he-goats so she could prepare for his father the kind of meal he liked.
He went after his mother until he came to the land of Kabratan, and he lived there.{o}

Rachel gave birth to a son during the night and called him “Son of my sorrow,” because the birth had caused her such pain. But his father named him Benjamin, on the eleventh of the eighth month, in the first year of the sixth week of this jubilee.{p}
Rachel died there and was buried in the land of Ephrath, which is Bethlehem, and Jacob built a pillar on Rachel’s grave, on the road above her grave.

notes.text: Testament of Levi 8 puts Levi’s vision of seven men in white at Bethel. “Priest of the Most High God” is also Melchizedek’s title (Gen 14:18), later taken up by the Maccabean priest-kings; see also Ps 110:4.
The fourteenth of the seventh month: about October 3.
Counting backward from Benjamin (1) to Levi (10th), Levi is the tenth and so the tithe (Lev 27:32). “Filled his hands” is the technical term for ordination as a priest (Ex 29:9).
The fifteenth of the seventh month, about October 4, is the Feast of Tabernacles. The numbers of animals do not match Num 29:12–40.
That is, the people and servants of his household who were counted in the tithe, as Testament of Levi 9 says.
The second tithe: Deut 14:23.
The twenty-second of the seventh month: about October 11, the eighth day after the start of Tabernacles.
Here the promise covers the whole inhabited earth, not only the land of Canaan as in Gen 35:12.
Compare 4 Ezra 14:24.
The Bethel sanctuary is not to be the one central shrine. Compare 45:4.
Compare 4 Ezra 14:40 and John 14:26.

This is the eighth day of Tabernacles (Lev 23:36). The Hebrew name is aseret, “assembly” or “holding back.” The Ethiopic text is corrupt here; Charles suggests “keeping back,” because he was kept back on that day.
The text of this verse is very damaged. The sense is that the eighth day is counted among the festal days of the year.
The twenty-third of the seventh month: about October 12. Compare Gen 35:8.
This place name comes from a misunderstanding of Hebrew kibrath ha’arets, “some distance,” in Gen 35:16.
Eighth month, day 11: about October 30. The year is 2143 from creation in Charles’s count. Benjamin means “son of the right hand” or “of the south”; Ben-oni, “son of my sorrow.”

chapters.heading: Levi’s Dream, the Tithes, and Israel’s Name

verses.text: Jacob went and lived to the south of Magdaladra’ef, and he went to his father Isaac, he and his wife Leah, on the new moon of the tenth month.{a}
Reuben saw Bilhah, Rachel’s maid, his father’s concubine, bathing in water in a secret place, and he desired her.
He hid himself at night, and entered Bilhah’s house, and found her sleeping alone on a bed in her house.
He lay with her, and she woke and saw that Reuben was lying with her in the bed, and she pulled the edge of her covering and seized him, and cried out, and discovered that it was Reuben.
She was ashamed because of him, and released her hand from him, and he fled.
She lamented greatly over this thing and did not tell anyone.

When Jacob returned and sought her, she said to him, “I am not clean for you, for I have been defiled as far as you are concerned; for Reuben has defiled me and lain with me in the night, and I was asleep and did not know until he uncovered my skirt and slept with me.”
Jacob was very angry with Reuben because he had lain with Bilhah, because he had uncovered his father’s skirt.
Jacob did not go near her again because Reuben had defiled her. And any man who uncovers his father’s skirt does a very wicked deed, for he is abominable before the Lord.

For this reason the heavenly tablets contain this written decree: no man may sleep with his father’s wife or lift the edge of his father’s robe, for that is defiling. Both are certain to die, the man who sleeps with his father’s wife and the woman too, because they have polluted the land.
There will be nothing unclean before our God in the nation he has chosen for himself as a possession.
A second time it is written: “Cursed is the man who lies with his father’s wife, for he has exposed his father’s shame.” And all the Lord’s holy ones said, “So be it, so be it.”

You, Moses, command the children of Israel to keep this word; for it carries the penalty of death; and it is unclean, and there is no atonement forever to atone for the man who has done this, but he is to be put to death, killed, stoned, and rooted out from the midst of the people of our God.
No man in Israel who does this may stay alive even one day on earth, for he is loathsome and impure.
Let them not say that Reuben was granted life and forgiveness after he lay with his father’s concubine, and she also, though she had a husband, and her husband Jacob, his father, was still alive.

For until that time the ordinance, judgment, and law had not been revealed in full for everyone, but in your days it has been revealed as a law of seasons and days, and an everlasting law for the everlasting generations.{b}
For this law there is no end of days and no atonement; but both must be rooted out from the midst of the nation; on the day they commit it, they shall kill them.

You, Moses, write it down for Israel so that they keep it and act according to these words and do not commit a sin unto death; for the Lord our God is judge, who shows no favoritism and accepts no gifts.

Tell them these words of the covenant, so that they hear and keep them and are on their guard concerning them, and are not destroyed and rooted out of the land; for all who commit it on the earth are uncleanness, abomination, contamination, and pollution before our God.

There is no greater sin than the fornication they commit on the earth; for Israel is a holy nation to the Lord its God, a nation of inheritance, a priestly and royal nation and his own possession; and no such uncleanness will appear in the midst of the holy nation.
In the third year of this sixth week Jacob and all his sons went and lived in the house of Abraham, near his father Isaac and his mother Rebecca.{c}

These were the names of Jacob’s sons: the firstborn Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun, the sons of Leah; and the sons of Rachel, Joseph and Benjamin; and the sons of Bilhah, Dan and Naphtali; and the sons of Zilpah, Gad and Asher; and Dinah, Leah’s daughter, the only daughter of Jacob.
They came and bowed to Isaac and Rebecca, and when they saw them they blessed Jacob and all his sons, and Isaac rejoiced greatly, for he saw the sons of his younger son Jacob, and he blessed them.

notes.text: The new moon of the tenth month is the first day of the tenth month, about December 20, a Wednesday. The place name stands for “the tower of Eder of Ephrath” (Gen 35:21).
Compare Rom 4:15: “where there is no law there is no transgression.”
Year 2145 from creation in Charles’s count.

chapters.heading: Reuben and Bilhah; Laws on Incest

verses.text: In the sixth year of this week of this forty-fourth jubilee Jacob sent his sons to pasture their sheep, and his servants with them, in the pastures of Shechem.{a}
The seven kings of the Amorites gathered against them to kill them, hiding under the trees, and to take their cattle as plunder.{b}

Jacob, Levi, Judah, and Joseph were in the house with their father Isaac, for his spirit was sorrowful and they could not leave him; and Benjamin, the youngest, stayed with his father for that reason.

Then came the king of Taphu, the king of Aresa, the king of Seragan, the king of Selo, the king of Ga’as, the king of Bethhoron, the king of Ma’anisakir, and all those who live in these mountains and in the woods in the land of Canaan.{c}
They told Jacob, “Look, the Amorite kings have surrounded your sons and plundered their herds.”
He got up from his house, he and his three sons and all his father’s servants and his own servants, and went against them with six thousand men carrying swords.

He killed them in the pastures of Shechem, and pursued those who fled, and he killed them with the edge of the sword, and he killed Aresa, Taphu, Seragan, Selo, Ma’anisakir, and Ga’as, and recovered his herds.{d}
He prevailed over them and imposed tribute on them, that they should pay him tribute of five fruit products of their land, and he built Robel and Tamnatares.{e}
He came back safely and made terms with them, and they were his subjects until the day he and his sons went down into Egypt.
In the seventh year of this week he sent Joseph from his house to the region of Shechem to see how his brothers were, and Joseph found them near Dothan.

They dealt treacherously with him and made a plot against him to kill him, but changing their minds, they sold him to Ishmaelite merchants, and they brought him down to Egypt and sold him to Potiphar, Pharaoh’s official, the chief of the cooks, priest of the city of Elew.{f}
The sons of Jacob killed a kid and dipped Joseph’s coat in the blood and sent it to their father Jacob on the tenth of the seventh month.{g}

He mourned the whole night, since they had brought him the news at evening. Grief made him feverish over the death, and he said, “A wild animal has eaten Joseph.” Everyone in his household wept and mourned with him throughout that day.
His sons and his daughter got up to comfort him, but he refused to be comforted for his son.

On that day Bilhah heard that Joseph had perished, and she died mourning him; she was living in Kabratan, and Dinah his daughter also died after Joseph perished. And these three mournings came on Israel in one month.
They buried Bilhah opposite Rachel’s tomb, and Dinah his daughter they buried there too.
He mourned for Joseph one year, and did not stop, for he said, “Let me go down to the grave mourning for my son.”

For this reason it is ordained for the children of Israel that they should humble themselves on the tenth of the seventh month, the day the news that made Jacob weep for Joseph reached him, and that they should make atonement for themselves on it with a young goat on the tenth of the seventh month, once a year, for their sins; for they had grieved their father’s love over his son Joseph.{h}
This day has been ordained so that they should grieve on it for their sins, for all their transgressions and all their errors, so that they might cleanse themselves on that day once a year.

After Joseph perished, Jacob’s sons took wives for themselves. The name of Reuben’s wife was Ada; the name of Simeon’s wife was Adiba’a, a Canaanite; the name of Levi’s wife was Melka, of the daughters of Aram, of the descendants of the sons of Terah; the name of Judah’s wife, Betasu’el, a Canaanite; the name of Issachar’s wife, Hezaqa; the name of Zebulun’s wife, Ni’iman; the name of Dan’s wife, ’Egla; the name of Naphtali’s wife, Rasu’u, of Mesopotamia; the name of Gad’s wife, Maka; the name of Asher’s wife, Ijona; the name of Joseph’s wife, Asenath the Egyptian; and the name of Benjamin’s wife, ’Ijasaka.{i}
Simeon repented and took a second wife from Mesopotamia, as his brothers did.

notes.text: Charles dates this to 2148 from creation.
The war story is told more fully in the Testament of Judah 3–7. It fits Gen 48:22, where Jacob says he took Shechem with sword and bow.

Taphu is probably Tappuah. Aresa may be Hazor. Selo is Shiloh. Bethhoron was the scene of several Maccabean victories (1 Macc 3:13–24). Several of these places are famous from Maccabean battles, which may be why the author names them.
Six of the seven kings are killed; so also the Testament of Judah 4.
Timnath-heres, as in Judg 2:9.
The Greek calls Potiphar “chief cook” by mistaking the Hebrew (“captain of the guard”). Elew is Heliopolis (On), the Egyptian temple city.
The tenth of the seventh month: about September 29, a Friday in this calendar.
This reason for the Day of Atonement (Lev 16) is peculiar to Jubilees. “Humble themselves” means to fast.
Betasu’el is “daughter of Shua” (Gen 38:2). Compare Testament of Levi 11. These marriages with Canaanites conflict with 30:7–10.

chapters.heading: War with the Amorite Kings; Joseph Sold; the Day of Atonement

verses.text: In the first year of the first week of the forty-fifth jubilee Rebecca called her son Jacob and commanded him concerning his father and his brother, that he should honor them all the days of his life.{a}
Jacob said, “I will do everything as you have commanded me; for this will be honor and greatness to me, and righteousness before the Lord, that I should honor them.
You too, mother, know from the time I was born until this day all my deeds and everything in my heart, that I always think good toward everyone.
How could I not do this thing you have commanded me, that I should honor my father and my brother?
Tell me, mother, what perversity have you seen in me, and I will turn away from it, and mercy will be on me.”

She answered, “My son, in all my days I have seen nothing twisted in you, only what is right. Still, let me tell you plainly: I am going to die this year and will not outlive it. I saw the day of my death in a dream, and I am not to live past a hundred and fifty-five years. Look, I have used up all the days I was given to live.”

Jacob laughed at his mother’s words, because his mother had told him that she would die; and she was sitting opposite him in full strength, and was not weak; for she came and went and saw, and her teeth were strong, and no illness had touched her all the days of her life.

Jacob said to her, “Blessed am I, mother, if my days come near the days of your life, and my strength stays with me as yours does; and you will not die, for you are joking idly with me about your death.”

She went in to Isaac and said to him, “I make one request of you: make Esau swear that he will not harm Jacob or pursue him with enmity; for you know Esau’s thoughts, that they have been perverse from his youth, and there is no goodness in him; for he wants you dead, to kill him.

You know everything he has done from the day his brother Jacob went to Haran until this day: how he has abandoned us with his whole heart and done evil to us; he has taken your flocks for himself and carried off all your possessions from before your face.
When we begged and pleaded with him for what was our own, he acted like a man doing us a favor.

He is bitter against you because you blessed Jacob, your perfect and upright son; for there is no evil in him, only goodness, and since he came from Haran until this day he has not robbed us of anything, for he brings us everything in its season always, and rejoices with all his heart when we take from his hands, and he blesses us, and has not left us since he came from Haran until this day, and he stays with us continually at home, honoring us.”

Isaac said to her, “I also know and see what Jacob does, how he honors us wholeheartedly. I used to love Esau more than Jacob because he was the firstborn, but now I love Jacob more, since Esau has done many wicked things and has no justice in him: every one of his ways is wrongdoing and violence.

Now my heart is troubled because of all his deeds, and neither he nor his descendants will be saved, for they are those who will be destroyed from the earth and rooted out from under heaven, for he has abandoned the God of Abraham and gone after his wives and after their uncleanness and their error, he and his children.
You tell me to make him swear that he will not kill his brother Jacob; even if he swears, he will not keep his oath, and he will do no good but only evil.
But if he wants to kill his brother Jacob, he will be given into Jacob’s hands, and will not escape from his hands.
Do not be afraid for Jacob, for Jacob’s guardian is great, powerful, honored, and praised more than Esau’s guardian.”{b}
Rebecca sent and called Esau, and he came to her, and she said to him, “I have a request to make of you, my son, and promise to do it, my son.”
He said, “I will do everything you say to me, and I will not refuse your request.”

She said to him, “I ask that on the day I die you will take me in and bury me near Sarah, your father’s mother, and that you and Jacob will love each other, and that neither will want evil against the other, but only mutual love, and so you will prosper, my sons, and be honored in the midst of the land, and no enemy will rejoice over you, and you will be a blessing and a mercy in the eyes of all who love you.”
He said, “I will do all you have told me, and I will bury you on the day you die near Sarah, my father’s mother, as you desire that her bones be near your bones.

And my brother Jacob I will love above every other person, since I have no brother in the whole world except him. There is no great virtue in my loving him: he is my brother, we were planted together in your body and came out together from your womb. If I did not love my brother, whom would I love?
I myself beg you to exhort Jacob concerning me and my sons, for I know that he will surely be king over me and my sons, for on the day my father blessed him he made him the higher and me the lower.
I swear to you that I will love him, and not want evil against him all the days of my life, but only good.” And he swore to her about all this matter.
She called Jacob before Esau’s eyes and gave him a commandment according to the words she had spoken to Esau.
He said, “I will do what pleases you; believe me that no evil will come from me or my sons against Esau, and I will be first in nothing but love.”

They ate and drank, she and her sons, that night, and she died that night, three jubilees and one week and one year old, and her two sons Esau and Jacob buried her in the double cave near Sarah, their father’s mother.{c}

notes.text: Year 2157 from creation in Charles’s count.
“Guardian” here is a guardian angel; compare Matt 18:10; Acts 12:15.
3 × 49 + 7 + 1 = 155 years. The double cave is Machpelah.

chapters.heading: Rebecca’s Last Words and Death

verses.text: In the sixth year of this week Isaac summoned his two sons, Esau and Jacob. When they came he told them, “My sons, I am about to take the road my fathers took, to the everlasting home where they are.{a}
So bury me near my father Abraham, in the double cave in the field of Ephron the Hittite, where Abraham bought a tomb to bury in; in the tomb that I dug for myself, bury me there.
I command you, my sons, to practice righteousness and uprightness on the earth, so that the Lord may bring on you all that the Lord said he would do for Abraham and his descendants.
Love each other, my sons, the way a person loves his own life. Let each look for ways to help his brother, and let them work together in the land, loving one another as they love themselves.
Concerning idols, I command and warn you to reject them and hate them and not love them, for they are full of deception for those who worship them and bow down to them.

Remember, my sons, the Lord God of your father Abraham, and how I too worshiped him and served him in righteousness and joy, so that he might multiply you and increase your descendants like the stars of heaven, and establish you on the earth as the plant of righteousness that will not be rooted out through all generations forever.

Now I will make you swear a great oath, for there is no oath greater than it, by the glorious, honored, great, splendid, wonderful, and mighty name, which created the heavens and earth and all things together, that you will fear him and worship him.

And that each of you will love his brother with affection and righteousness, and that neither of you will want evil against his brother from now on forever, all the days of your life, so that you may prosper in all your deeds and not be destroyed.

If either of you plots evil against his brother, know that from now on everyone who plots evil against his brother will fall into his hand and be rooted out of the land of the living, and his descendants will be destroyed from under heaven.

On the day of confusion, of cursing, fury, and anger, with blazing, consuming fire, just as he burned Sodom, so he will burn that man’s land and town and everything he owns. He will be wiped from the book of human instruction and not entered in the book of life, but in the book marked for destruction. He will depart into an everlasting curse, so that their sentence is renewed forever in hatred, cursing, rage, torment, fury, plagues, and sickness.
I say and testify to you, my sons, according to the judgment that will come on the man who wants to injure his brother.”

He divided all his possessions between the two on that day, and he gave the larger portion to the firstborn, together with the tower and everything around it, and everything Abraham had possessed at the Well of the Oath.
He said, “This larger portion I will give to the firstborn.”
Esau said, “I sold my birthright to Jacob and gave it to him; let it be given to him, and I have nothing to say about it, for it is his.”

Isaac said, “May a blessing rest on you, my sons, and on your descendants this day, for you have given me rest, and my heart is not pained about the birthright, lest you work wickedness because of it.
May the Most High God bless the man who works righteousness, him and his descendants forever.”

When he had finished instructing and blessing them, they ate and drank together in his presence. He was glad that the two were of one mind. They left him, spent the rest of the day at rest, and went to sleep.

That day Isaac lay down on his bed, glad at heart, and fell into the everlasting sleep, dying at a hundred and eighty. He had lived twenty-five weeks of years and five years. His two sons, Esau and Jacob, buried him.{b}
Esau went to the land of Edom, to the mountains of Seir, and lived there.

Jacob lived in the mountains of Hebron, in the tower of the land of the wanderings of his father Abraham, and he worshiped the Lord with all his heart and according to the visible commands, as he had divided the days of his generations.{c}

Leah, his wife, died in the fourth year of the second week of the forty-fifth jubilee. He buried her in the twin cave next to his mother Rebecca, on the left of the tomb of Sarah, his father’s mother.{d}
All her sons and his sons came to mourn over his wife Leah with him, and to comfort him about her, for he was lamenting her.

For he loved her very much after her sister Rachel died; for she was perfect and upright in all her ways and honored Jacob, and all the days she lived with him he did not hear a harsh word from her mouth, for she was gentle, peaceable, upright, and honorable.
He remembered all her deeds that she had done during her life, and he lamented her greatly; for he loved her with all his heart and all his soul.

notes.text: Year 2162 from creation in Charles’s count. “Eternal house” is the grave; compare Eccl 12:5.
The commands were made visible to Jacob on the seven tablets that the angel showed him (32:21). “Most High God” (verse 16) is a favorite title in this book, in Sirach, Daniel, and 4 Ezra.
Year 2167 from creation in Charles’s count.

chapters.heading: Isaac’s Last Words and Death; the Death of Leah

verses.text: On the day that Isaac, the father of Jacob and Esau, died, the sons of Esau heard that Isaac had given the elder’s portion to his younger son Jacob, and they were very angry.{a}
They quarreled with their father, saying, “Why has your father given Jacob the elder’s portion and passed over you, although you are the elder and Jacob the younger?”

He told them, “I traded my birthright to Jacob for a bowl of lentil stew. Then, the day my father sent me out to hunt game and bring him something to eat so he could bless me, Jacob came in with a trick and brought my father food and drink. My father blessed him and made me his subject.
Now our father has made us swear, me and him, that we will not plot evil against each other, but will continue in love and peace, each with his brother, and not make our ways corrupt.”

They said to him, “We will not listen to you to make peace with him; for our strength is greater than his, and we are more powerful than he; we will go against him and kill him and destroy him and his sons. And if you will not go with us, we will do harm to you too.

Now listen to us: let us send to Aram, Philistia, Moab, and Ammon, and choose for ourselves chosen men who are eager for battle, and let us go against him and fight him, and exterminate him from the earth before he grows strong.”{b}
Their father said to them, “Do not go and do not make war with him, or you will fall before him.”
They said to him, “This too is exactly how you have behaved from your youth until this day, and you put your neck under his yoke. We will not listen to these words.”
They sent to Aram and to Aduram, the friend of their father, and hired a thousand fighting men with them, chosen men of war.

From Moab and from the Ammonites came a thousand hired chosen men, and from Philistia a thousand chosen men of war, and from Edom and the Horites a thousand chosen fighting men, and from the Kittim mighty men of war.
They said to their father, “Go out with them and lead them, or we will kill you.”
He burned with rage when he saw that his sons were pushing him to march in front of them against his brother Jacob.

But afterward he remembered all the evil lying hidden in his heart against his brother Jacob; and he did not remember the oath he had sworn to his father and mother that he would never plot evil against his brother Jacob.

In spite of all this, Jacob did not know they were coming against him to battle, and he was mourning for his wife Leah, until they came very near the tower with four thousand warriors and chosen men of war.

The people of Hebron sent him word: “Your brother is marching against you to fight, with four thousand swordsmen carrying shields and weapons.” They sent this because they preferred Jacob to Esau; Jacob was the more generous and kind of the two.
But Jacob would not believe it until they came very near the tower.

He shut the gates of the tower, and stood on the battlements and spoke to his brother Esau and said, “Noble is the comfort with which you have come to comfort me for my wife who has died. Is this the oath you swore to your father and again to your mother before they died? You have broken the oath, and at the moment you swore to your father you were condemned.”

Then Esau answered and said to him, “Neither human beings nor the animals of the earth have any oath of righteousness that, once sworn, holds forever; every day they plot evil against each other, and how each may kill his adversary and enemy.
You hate me and my children forever. There is no keeping the tie of brotherhood with you.

Hear what I now declare to you: only if the boar can change its hide and turn its bristles soft as wool, or grow horns on its head like a stag’s or a ram’s, will I honor the bond of brotherhood with you. {c}
If wolves make peace with lambs so as not to devour or harm them, and if their hearts are good toward them, then there will be peace in my heart toward you.
If the lion becomes the friend of the ox and makes peace with him, and is bound under one yoke with him and plows with him, then I will make peace with you.

When the raven becomes white as the raza, then know that I have loved you and will make peace with you. You will be rooted out, and your sons will be rooted out, and there will be no peace for you.”{d}

When Jacob saw that Esau was so evilly disposed toward him with his heart and all his soul as to kill him, and that he had come springing like the wild boar that charges on the spear that pierces and kills it and does not recoil from it,
he spoke to his own men and to his servants that they should attack him and all his companions.

notes.text: The story of the war between Jacob’s sons and Esau, in chapters 37 and 38, is also found in Testament of Judah 9 and in later Jewish tradition; Jubilees has the oldest form. Several peoples named here played a part in Maccabean wars.
Aram is Syria, the ruling power in the Maccabean period.
Sayings of this kind compare with the rebuke to Akiba: “Sooner will grass grow on your beard than the Messiah appear.” The boar may stand for Esau.
The raza is a large white bird said to eat grasshoppers.

chapters.heading: Esau’s Sons Make War on Jacob

verses.text: After that Judah spoke to his father Jacob and said to him, “Bend your bow, father, and shoot your arrows and bring down the adversary and kill the enemy; and may you have the power, for we will not kill your brother, since he is like you and the same as you; let us give him this honor.”
Then Jacob bent his bow and shot the arrow and struck his brother Esau on his right breast and killed him.{a}
Again he shot an arrow and struck Adoran the Aramean on the left breast, and drove him backward and killed him.
Then Jacob’s sons went out, they and their servants, dividing themselves into companies on the four sides of the tower.
Judah led the way, with Naphtali, Gad, and fifty servants at his side, to the south of the tower. They struck down everyone in front of them, and no one got away.
Levi, Dan, and Asher went out on the east side of the tower, and fifty men with them, and they killed the fighting men of Moab and Ammon.
Reuben, Issachar, and Zebulun went out on the north side of the tower, and fifty men with them, and they killed the fighting men of the Philistines.

Simeon, Benjamin, and Enoch, Reuben’s son, went out on the west side of the tower, and fifty men with them, and they killed four hundred men of Edom and the Horites, stout warriors; and six hundred fled, and four of Esau’s sons fled with them, and left their father lying dead, where he had fallen on the hill that is in Aduram.{b}
Jacob’s sons pursued them to the mountains of Seir. Jacob buried his brother on the hill that is in Aduram, and he returned to his house.
Jacob’s sons leaned hard on Esau’s sons in the highlands of Seir and bent their necks, so that they became servants to Jacob’s sons.
They sent to their father to ask whether they should make peace with them or kill them.
Jacob sent word to his sons to make peace. They did so and laid the yoke of servitude on the Edomites, who paid tribute to Jacob and his sons from then on.
They continued to pay tribute to Jacob until the day he went down to Egypt.
The sons of Edom have not got free of the yoke of servitude that the twelve sons of Jacob put on them, to this day.{c}
These are the kings who reigned in Edom before any king reigned over the children of Israel, in the land of Edom.
Balaq, son of Beor, reigned in Edom, and the name of his city was Danaba.{d}
Balaq died, and Jobab, son of Zara of Boser, reigned in his place.
Jobab died, and ’Asam of the land of Teman reigned in his place.
’Asam died, and ’Adath, son of Barad, who killed Midian in the field of Moab, reigned in his place, and the name of his city was Avith.
’Adath died, and Salman from ’Amaseqa reigned in his place.
Salman died, and Saul of Ra’aboth by the river reigned in his place.
Saul died, and Ba’elunan, son of Achbor, reigned in his place.
Ba’elunan, son of Achbor, died, and ’Adath reigned in his place, and the name of his wife was Maitabith, daughter of Matarat, daughter of Metabedza’ab.
These are the kings who reigned in the land of Edom.

notes.text: Later tradition says Esau was killed by Chushim, son of Dan, at Machpelah, when Jacob’s body was brought there for burial.
Aduram is the Adora of 1 Macc 13:20 in Edom, captured by John Hyrcanus, who forced the Edomites to accept circumcision. In Testament of Judah 9 the name appears as Anoniram.
“To this day” is the author’s own day; Edom was made tributary to Israel by John Hyrcanus.
These names follow Gen 36:31–39 in the Greek form. Balaq is Bela; Danaba is Dinhabah.

chapters.heading: The Battle at the Tower and the Kings of Edom

verses.text: Jacob lived in the land of his father’s wanderings, in the land of Canaan.
These are the generations of Jacob. Joseph was seventeen years old when they took him down to the land of Egypt, and Potiphar, Pharaoh’s official, the chief cook, bought him.{a}
He set Joseph over all his house, and the blessing of the Lord came on the Egyptian’s house because of Joseph, and the Lord made him prosper in everything he did.
The Egyptian committed everything into Joseph’s hands, for he saw that the Lord was with him and that the Lord made him prosper in everything he did.
Joseph’s appearance was handsome, very beautiful was his appearance, and his master’s wife lifted up her eyes and saw Joseph, and she loved him and begged him to be with her.

But he did not surrender himself. He remembered the Lord, and what his father Jacob used to read to him from Abraham’s teachings: that no man may commit adultery with a married woman, that death is the penalty fixed for him in heaven before God Most High, and that his sin will be entered against him in the eternal books before the Lord forever.
Joseph remembered these words and refused to lie with her.
She begged him for a year, but he refused and would not listen.

But she threw her arms around him and clung to him inside the house, trying to force him to lie with her. She had shut the doors. He left his cloak in her hands, burst through the door, and ran out of her sight.

The woman saw that he would not lie with her, and she slandered him in the presence of her lord, saying, “Your Hebrew servant, whom you love, tried to force me so that he might lie with me; and when I raised my voice he fled and left his garment in my hands when I held him, and he broke through the door.”
The Egyptian saw Joseph’s garment and the broken door and heard his wife’s words, and he threw Joseph into prison, into the place where the prisoners the king imprisoned were kept.
He stayed there in the prison, and the Lord granted Joseph the goodwill and pity of the chief jailer, who saw that the Lord was with him and made all his work succeed.
He committed everything into his hands, and the chief of the prison guards knew nothing of what was with him, for Joseph did everything, and the Lord brought it to completion.

He stayed there two years. In those days Pharaoh, king of Egypt, was angry with his two officials, the chief butler and the chief baker, and he put them in custody in the house of the chief cook, in the prison where Joseph was kept.
The chief of the prison guards appointed Joseph to serve them, and he served them.
The two of them had a dream, the chief cupbearer and the chief baker, and they told it to Joseph.
